extra.bslay_tactic_text:
When the Araxxi encounter begins, you'll be contained within a starting area.
To progress you must pick one of the two burnable webs to set fire to. After a minute the web will burn away and you can progress to stage two. The webs you can burn change every four days.

In this stage Araxxor can Cocoon, Cleave and Web Shield.

There are three types of styles that Araxxor can spawn in, Ranged represented by green legs, and will apply a poison dot throughout the fight, Magic represented by blue legs, and damage throughout the fight will slowly drain stats and lower overload timers and Melee represented by red legs, and will apply a damage over time effect that increases randomly throughout the effect's lifetime.

When fired, you will become encased in webbing. The more you click the more you will break free. Using the ability <col=E6DCB4>Freedom</col> or <col=E6DCB4>Anticipation</col> before this attack will help lower the amount you are cocooned for.

A web shielding will cover the boss for 10 seconds. While this is present, the boss will take half damage and reflect half damage to you. If you don't attack, the boss will heal while the shield is present.
The boss will pull you towards them if you haven't used the <col=E6DCB4>Freedom</col> or <col=E6DCB4>Anticipation</col> ability. Cleave will hit massive damage to anyone caught in front of the boss.

After the web has burned away, you can venture down your chosen path. Depending on what path you choose, Araxxor will gain new attacks. You'll have to deal with these before progressing to Stage Three.

In all paths, Araxxor will spawn a few eggs which will hatch into aggressive spiders if not dealt with. Luckily he'll also launch a fiery projectile towards you. If this explodes on the eggs it will destroy them - enraging the boss!

If you take the top path, Araxxor will try and spawn spiders to help kill you. Other than standard spiders, he can spawn a <col=FFFFFF>pulsing spider</col> that will heal him while it lives, and a <col=FFFFFF>mirrorback spider</col> that will make the boss reflect all damage while the mirrorback is alive.

If you take the middle path, Araxxor can fire a projectile at the floor leaving an acidic puddle on the floor for ten seconds.

After this time the puddle will form into an acidic spider that will rush towards you, exploding for massive damage after a short amount of time or if it touches you.

On path two you must degrade the ramp to progress to Stage Three. To do this you must have Araxxor stay in the acid pool to absorb the acid.

You need him to have at least half the acid to degrade the ramp - note that it will drip off him if he isn't in the pool.
If you take path three, Araxxor will plunge the entire area into darkness which will inflict increasing damage over time if you do not stand in the light beams.

Roughly every minute in path three, Araxxor will drop down from the ceiling and charge you. If you make an attempt to dodge he'll smash into the wall behind.

Dodging in the correct direction prevents you from taking damage and causes the most damage to the wall, with only two being required for the wall to cave in.

On entry to stage three, Araxxor will prioritise finishing off any path mechanics you didn't finish. He may spawn acid spiders if you chose path two and spiders if you chose path one.

On top of this, the path you didn't pick will become active, so those attacks will occur in stage 3 until Araxxor dies.

After you have defeated Araxxor, Araxxi will consume him. Araxxi will use any left over attacks (such as acid or spider minions) as well as performing Cleave, Web Shield and Cocoon.

As Araxxi drops below 50% health she will stop doing special attacks and instead grow increasingly damaging.

As Araxxi goes below 25% health (or 35% in duo), she will enrage faster and spawn an acid wave that tracks the target down until they are hit. When the acid wave hits, it will remain on the target until they move away, at which point it will bounce away and start again.

In the Barrows, there are six barrow mounds. Each leads to a crypt which contains one of the infamous Barrows Brothers. One of the brothers won't be present and instead his grave will give access to the area beneath the crypts.

In the area beneath the crypts you'll have a chance to encounter any brothers you've not killed. Navigating to the centre will grant access to the reward chest.
The more Barrows Brothers you kill, the better chance you'll have to receive loot!

Ahrim is a mage of great strength and will attack with powerful fire spells.
There is a 1/4 chance with every attack that Ahrim will drain your Strength level.
Dharok wields a massive greataxe. As he attacks you, he'll hit harder the lower his life points are. Protecting for melee or staying at a distance is recommended.
Guthan uses his warspear to sap health from his victims. With every attack there is a 1/4 chance he'll heal what he hits!
Karil is a strong ranger and uses his repeating crossbow to deal damage. There is a 1/4 chance he'll drain your Magic level if he hits you.
Torag uses his massive hammer to smash his foes. There is a 1/4 chance his melee attacks will drain 5% of your Adrenaline.
Verac wears unholy armour that grants his warmace a 1/4 chance to ignore his opponent's armour!
Akrisae the Doomed is located north in Verac's tomb. Those who fight him should be prepared - he can pray against your attacks and switch styles in reaction to your attacks.

At the start of the encounter, the shadow binds the brothers together. If a brother is defeated, you must defeat another within 30 seconds or the shadow will revive all brothers to fight once more. Defeating a brother will also reset the revive timers of other brothers, and it will heal any brother still standing.

At the start of the fight one brother will be more in contact with the Shadow Realm and there is a chance he will send all players to the Shadow Realm at a point in the fight.

Inside the Shadow Realm, all special attacks the brothers perform will have increased accuracy and damage.
Be warned! If no-one is present on one side of the encounter, the shadow will send all brothers to the other side, when they are all back up.

Ahrim will use standard fire attacks against his opponent that have a 1/8 chance to drain Strength levels. He also uses the <col=FFFFFF>Flight, Telejump, Shadow Pits</col>, and <col=FFFFFF>Turret of Fire</col> special attacks.
When Ahrim drops below 90% life points, he'll take the air. When flying, Ahrim will only use standard attacks against you. While flying Ahrim is immune to melee damage and takes 50% magic damage.
Ahrim will Telejump to a pillar in the centre of the arena and begin attacking the other side of the encounter - as well as lighting all the shadow pits on the other side.
When Ahrim sets a pit to shadow, it'll glow brightly and hurt anyone caught in it. There is a 1/8 chance Ahrim's pit will be red. Any brother that walks in a red shadow pit will heal.
Ahrim will teleport to a spot in the room and ignite his hands. As he rotates on the spot, anyone caught in the flames will take heavy fire damage.

Dharok uses damaging melee attacks that get far stronger the fewer life points he has.

Dharok can use the Greatest Axe, Wall Slam, and Hurricane special attacks.
Dharok raises his greataxe for <col=FFFFFF>10</col> seconds, storing any damage in it that is done against him. After the 10 seconds, he'll unleash it on his next attack!
Dharok runs to a nearby wall, runs up it and then flings himself towards his original target, slamming down for massive damage.
Dharok starts spinning wildly towards his opponent, hitting all nearby with his greataxe for heavy damage.

Guthan uses his warspear, which has a 1/8 chance to heal an amount equal to his hit.

Guthan can use the Impale, Hurricane, and Throw special attacks.
Guthan will try to throw his spear at a player he isn't targetting. If the spear impales the target they will bleed for heavy damage, until they run to Guthan and he pulls it back out of them.
Guthan starts spinning wildly towards his opponent, hitting all nearby with his warspear for heavy damage.
Guthan will try to locate Ahrim, Karil, or Verac to throw them. If successful, he'll Surge over to them and throw them to a random nearby location, inflicting damage to anyone near where they land.

Karil uses his twin pistol crossbows to inflict ranged damage. There is a 1/8 chance his attacks will drain Attack and Magic levels.

Karil can also use the Portal Dash, Lightning Conductor and Bombard special attacks.

Karil will summon a shadow portal at his location that he uses to dash to the other side of the encounter.

He will continue jumping side-to-side until he runs out of portals. After 4 seconds the shadow portal will explode, dealing massive damage to those nearby, less if they are further away.

If you enter a shadow portal you will close it, preventing it from exploding but taking more damage if you have been through portals before.
Karil will teleport to a spot in the room and unleash shadow-lightning from his hands. As he rotates on the spot, anyone caught in the lightning will take heavy damage.

Karil will teleport to a pillar in the centre of the arena and begin attacking the other side of the encounter - as well as unleashing a massive lightning barrage down a strip of the room on the other side.

Torag uses his massive hammer to deal melee damage. He has a 1/8 chance to reduce his opponents' adrenaline by 5%, and can use the <col=FFFFFF>Hurricane, Throw, Wall Slam</col>, and <col=FFFFFF>Whack</col> special attacks.
Torag starts spinning wildly towards his opponent, hitting all adjacent with his hammer for heavy damage.
Torag will try to locate Ahrim, Karil, or Verac to throw them. If successful, he'll Surge over to them and throw them to a random nearby location, inflicting damage to anyone near where they land.
Torag runs to a nearby wall, runs up it and then flings himself towards his original target, slamming down for massive damage.

Torag will jump into air and smash his opponent from above, pushing them right through the ground! While stuck in the ground, Torag will constantly hit them - until someone else has hurt Torag enough that he stops!

Verac is back with his warmace. He will use standard attacks against you, with a 1/8 chance he'll ignore your armour when hitting.

Verac can also use the Wall Slam, Throw, Deathcopter, and Soulspot special attacks.
Verac runs to a nearby wall, runs up it and then flings himself towards his original target, slamming down for massive damage.
Verac will try to locate Ahrim or Karil to throw them. If successful, he'll Surge over to them and throw them to a random nearby location, inflicting damage to anyone near where they land.

Verac will signal to any of his brothers than he can launch in the next <col=FFFFFF>20 seconds</col>. If another brother tries to <col=FFFFFF>Throw</col> Verac in this time he will instead take to the air and track his opponent. Should he get to them he'll smash down for incredible damage.
Verac will tie his opponent's soul to a random point in the environment, marked by green arrows. Until his opponent stands on this spot, Verac will constantly sap their prayer points.

After the brothers have been defeated, you have to leave to claim any malevolent energy. As you leave the encounter area, it will begin to collapse, you and your team have <col=FFFFFF>30 seconds</col> to escape before it implodes.
The Chaos Elemental confuses his opponents, teleporting them to a random area around him unless they are more than 20m away.
The Chaos Elemental lets chaos decide when discord hits. When it meets its target, it will randomly act as a melee, ranged, or magic attack and hit as such.
If you have space in your inventory, the Chaos Elemental may use Madness against you. Madness aims to remove your main-hand weapon and up to three items in random slots.
Commander Zilyana smashes her sword against her target for heavy damage. There is a <col=FFFFFF>50%</col> chance when Zilyana attacks in melee that she instead performs her magical attack.
Commander Zilyana finds all nearby targets and calls upon Saradomin's lightning to deal heavy magic damage to all it hits.

Commander Zilyana has backup with her in the form of <col=FFFFFF>Bree, Starlight</col>, and <col=FFFFFF>Growler</col>. Each uses a different point of the combat triangle and Commander Zilyana will respawn any dead bodyguards every <col=FFFFFF>30 seconds.
Commander Zilyana summons a lightning storm on up to five opponents at a time. A lightning storm will move a small amount at random, hitting heavy magical damage to anyone caught in it.

When Commander Zilyana has been defeated for the second time, she can only be killed via use of an <col=FFFFFF>Ultimate ability.</col>. If this does not happen after <col=FFFFFF>6 seconds</col>, she will heal up and continue fighting.
The Corporeal Beast will violently swing his feet or stamp them at his target, hitting them for heavy damage with a chance to drain prayer points.

The Corporeal Beast hit its main target for heavy magic damage, also draining their prayer points, and degrading their summoning and magic levels. (If the targets summoning points are fully drained it will deal extra damage instead)

The Corporeal Beast fires a magical attack at his current target's position. On impact, it explodes and splits into multiple smaller projectiles - all hitting heavy magical damage to those get caught in the blast.
If the Corporeal Beast senses the presence of a familiar, he will devour it, destroying it completely.
Anyone caught standing up the Corporeal Beast will feel his wrath as he violently stomps on them, hitting heavy damage until they move away.

As the Corporeal Beast's life points drop, there is a greater chance he will spawn a dark core if one is not present.

A dark core will lock on to its target and fling itself towards it. Anyone caught on the dark core will take consistent damage that helps heal the Corporeal Beast.
Dagannoth Rex is the melee-based dagannoth king. He can only be hurt by <col=FFFFFF>magic</col> attacks.
Dagannoth Prime is the magic-based dagannoth king. He can only be hurt by <col=FFFFFF>ranged</col> attacks.
Dagannoth Supreme is the ranged-based dagannoth king. He can only be hurt by <col=FFFFFF>Melee</col> attacks.

Spinolyps can spawn all around the king's chamber in the water. They use a combination of magic and ranged attacks, which also have a chance of poisoning the player. Spinyolps can also dive and disappear into the water for a short time before re-emerging.
General Graardor punches his main target for massive melee damage.
General Graardor punches the ground in fury, sending the debris from the punch towards targets nearby for ranged damage.

General Graardor has backup with him in the form of <col=FFFFFF>Sergeant Strongstack, Steelwill</col>, and <col=FFFFFF>Grimspike</col>. Each uses a different combat style, and General Graardor will respawn any dead bodyguards every <col=FFFFFF>30 seconds.
The general goes into a defensive stance for <col=FFFFFF>10 seconds</col>. During this stance, the general reflects some of the damage he takes if inflicted from the front.

The general smashes his fists into the ground hitting anyone caught for heavy damage. Shortly after the ceiling crumbles down on the targets' locations. Those who can see the collapse risk taking damage from the debris if they are in the vicinity of its fall.
The Giant Mole slashes her main target for melee damage.
The Giant Mole will burrow into the ground and relocate herself to another area in the environment where she'll re-emerge and continue attacking when found.

The Giant Mole stomps the ground, loosening some of the ceiling. This attack will stun a main target and the mud from above will begin falling on them until they are freed, either by a team-mate or the mole herself.
The Giant Mole goes berserk for <col=FFFFFF>15 seconds</col>. During this time, the mole can be stunned and deals increased damage with increased accuracy.
When the Giant Mole is in the north-western room, she will summon smaller moles to aid her. The Giant Mole gains damage reduction if small moles are alive.
Har-Aken will emerge from the lava every <col=FFFFFF>30 seconds</col>. While it is visible, it can be attacked. After <col=FFFFFF>30 seconds</col> it will submerge once again.

While Har-Aken lives, its tentacles will spawn around the platform. These can spawn in <col=FFFFFF>magic</col> or <col=FFFFFF>ranged</col> forms, getting too close will allow them to <col=FFFFFF>melee</col> the target. These should be defeated to keep incoming damage as low as possible.

The Kalphite King will use abilities in between his special attacks.

If the Kalphite King is in melee form, he will use: Dismember, Hurricane Punish, Quake, and Slaughter.

If the Kalphite King is in Ranged form, he will use: Binding Shot, Ricochet, Bombardment, Fragmentation Shot, and Incendiary Shot.

If the Kalphite King is in magic form, he will use: Wrack, Impact, Combust, Chain and Wild Magic.
The Kalphite King charges forwards in his current direction, hitting all targets caught in his path for heavy damage, or higher damage if he slams them into a wall.

The Kalphite King prepares to kill his main target outright, putting all of their defensive abilities on hold. Another combatant is required to <col=E6DCB4>Provoke</col> the king off of his target and then prepare to soak/avoid the incoming damage themselves through use of <col=E6DCB4>defensive abilities</col>.
The Kalphite King attacks all targets directly in front of him for melee damage and knocks back those who are hit.

The Kalphite King burrows into the ground and disappears! Shortly after, he'll emerge from the ground where his current target is standing. Any person who is caught when he re-emerges will take large amounts of damage.

If the Kalphite King is hit with a stunning attack, he will use Freedom. Having to use freedom will also distract the king, delaying his next attack.

If the Kalphite King is hit with Tsunami,Pulverise, or Bombardment he may use Barricade, Immortality, or Rejuvenate.

:If the Kalphite King activates a red aura, he will heal himself for all damage he deals.

If the Kalphite King activates a green aura, he will heal himself for all damage he takes.

At certain points during the fight, as the Kalphite King lowers in health, he will summon swarms of kalphite guardians, strong magic users that will defend the king with magical attacks. Players standing on the ground where a guardian has burrowed will take melee damage when they surface.

At the start of the fight, the Kalphite Queen is grounded and will protect from all ranged and magical attacks.  During her grounded stage she will use the <col=FFFFFF>Bite, Claw, Lightning</col>, and <col=FFFFFF>Spines</col> special attacks.

After the Kalphite Queen is defeated she will hatch and begin her flying stage - in which she is immune to melee attacks.  During her flying stage she will continue to use <col=FFFFFF>Bite, Claw, Lightning</col>, and <col=FFFFFF>Spines</col> special attacks.
The Kalphite Queen bites her main target for melee damage.
The Kalphite Queen unleashes a barrage of lightning on all surround targets, hitting them for magical damage.
The Kalphite Queen launches a spine at every player nearby, hurting them with ranged damage.
The King Black Dragon will swipe or bite anyone who stands close to him during the fight.
Being a dragon, the King Black Dragon can use extremely powerful fire breath that will destroy anyone who does not bring the appropriate anti-fire protection.
The King Black Dragon can use a combined attack that hits with massive fire damage while freezing his opponent in place.
The King Black Dragon can use a combined attack that hits with massive fire damage and poisons his opponent.
The King Black Dragon can use a combined attack that hits massive fire damage and shocks his opponent, draining their skills and prayer points slightly.
Kree'arra fires tornadoes at nearby targets for heavy ranged damage with a chance to knockback any targets they hit. You can prevent the knockback by using the <col=E6DCB4>Anticipation</col> ability.
Kree'arra fires tornadoes at nearby targets for heavy Magic damage with a chance to knock back any targets they hit. You can prevent the knockback by using the <col=E6DCB4>Anticipation</col> ability.
Any targets who stand close to Kree'arra risk being hit by his heavy swipe attack.

Kree'arra has backup with him in the form of <col=FFFFFF>Wingman Skree, Flockleader Geerin</col>, and <col=FFFFFF>Flight Kilisa</col>. Each uses a different combat style and Kree'arra will respawn any dead bodyguards every <col=FFFFFF>30 seconds.

In Hard mode, Kree'arra calls on the power of his tornadoes in full, having vortexes appear in the room. Anyone caught in a vortex will take massive magic or ranged damage dependent on the type of vortex.

During Hard mode, Kree'arra will walk to the centre of the area and summon all vortexes to him. Anyone caught in the path of the tornado will take heavy damage. After Kree'arra has summoned them all to him he will disperse them again into the encounter.
K'ril uses his massive weapons to melee his primary target and inflict poisonous damage. If the target is protecting against melee attacks or he continues to miss he will start to get enraged.

K'ril uses his massive weapons to slam into the floor and unleash Magic damage on nearby targets. If the target is protecting against Magic attacks or he continues to miss he will start to get enraged.

After K'ril has had enough of his target defending or protecting against his attacks he'll leap into the air and smash down, hitting the main target for massive damage, hitting through prayers and draining prayer points.

K'ril has backup with him in the form of <col=FFFFFF>Tstanon Karlak, Zakl'n Gritch</col>, and <col=FFFFFF>Balfrug Kreeyath</col>. Each uses a different point of the combat triangle and K'ril will respawn any dead bodyguards every <col=FFFFFF>30 seconds.
K'ril looks at his main opponent and begins charging. Anyone caught in his charge takes massive damage until he hits a wall, stopping him in his tracks.
K'ril smashes his blade into the ground, which bursts into spikes from the impact. Standing in the spikes inflicts constant damage until the time out or you move off of them.
K'ril will enrage against his opponent and go into a crazed frenzy, swinging and chasing his target wildly. Anyone caught in his wild weapons will take double damage.

Legios use strong magic attacks, firing lightning at the floor at any targets who aren't moving.

Legio Primus will get stronger as his life points decrease.

Legios use strong magic attacks, firing lightning at the floor at any targets who aren't moving.

Legio Secundus will fire his lightning attack more often than his regular attacks as his life points get lower.

Legios use strong magic attacks, firing lightning at the floor at any targets who aren't moving.

Legio Tertius will summon rorarii, gladii, and capsarii as his life points lower to aid him.

Legios use strong magic attacks, firing lightning at the floor at any targets who aren't moving.

As his life points are lowered, Legio Quartus will teleport all targets straight towards him and fire an extra blast of lightning.

Legios use strong magic attacks, firing lightning at the floor at any targets who aren't moving.

As his lifepoints are lowered, Legio Quintus can create Lines of Ascension that draw across the arena and hurt anyone who dares cross them.

Legios use strong magic attacks, firing lightning at the floor at any targets who aren't moving.

Legio Sextus's lightning attack is far larger and lasts longer, making him a very potent legio.

Throughout the encounter, Nex will use a powerful sweeping melee attack against any targets within melee distance to her.

On her Zaros phase, Nex's melee attack will be expanded to a frontal cone.

During smoke phase, Nex will fire a barrage of smoky projectiles to all surrounding targets, hitting magical damage. There is also a chance Nex will use this attack to poison you, or pull you towards her if you haven't anticipated the attack.
Nex will infect one target with a virus. As that target coughs the virus away, they will infect any other targets adjacent to them. Every cough of the virus lowers combat stats.

Nex will align with Zaros, picking a path in the chamber to teleport to and firing herself forward to the centre. Any targets caught in the path or centre will be forced forward by her attack, taking massive damage.

When Nex drops below <col=FFFFFF>80% life points</col> she will call on Fumus to aid her. Until this point, Fumus is invulnerable. If Fumus is killed, Nex will move onto the next stage, calling on the power of Shadow.
During the Shadow phase, Nex will use the power of shadow to fling ranged projectiles at all surrounding targets.
Nex will find all nearby victims and put a deadly shadow below them. Shortly after placing the shadows, they will erupt, hitting heavy damage on anyone caught in the dark.

Nex will plunge her targets into darkness, making it darker the closer targets are to her. If any targets are too close to Nex for too long they will become engulfed in shadow, taking constant damage from the pure shadow.

When Nex drops below <col=FFFFFF>60% life points</col> she will call on Umbra to aid her. Until this point, Umbra is invulnerable. If Umbra is killed, Nex will move onto the next stage, calling on the power of blood.

Nex will use her wings to shield her from damage and siphon it to heal her. Any damage over time effects placed on Nex during blood phase will also heal her.

Any Blood reavers that are alive when Blood siphon starts will die and transfer their life points to Nex.

When Nex begins <col=FFFFFF>Blood Siphon</col>, she will also summon blood reavers to the arena. Any blood reavers that survive until the next <col=FFFFFF>Blood Siphon</col> will transfer their life points to Nex.
During the Blood phase, Nex will shoot Blood Barrage on her targets, healing a percentage of any damage it inflicts on them.

Nex will mark a target for sacrifice. This target has <col=FFFFFF>4 seconds</col> to get as far away from Nex as possible. If they do not manage to get far enough, Nex heals dramatically and instantly fires another <col=FFFFFF>Blood Barrage.</col>

When Nex drops below <col=FFFFFF>40% life points</col> she will call on Cruor to aid her. Until this point, Cruor is invulnerable. If Cruor is killed, Nex will move onto the next stage, calling on the power of ice.

Nex will put her target in a prison of ice. Other players have <col=FFFFFF>6 seconds</col> to free her prisoner before the ice shatters for massive damage. Other combatants can free the imprisoned player by destroying the icicles surrounding them.
During the Ice phase, Nex will use Ice Barrage against her targets, freezing them in place. Protection from Magic will help reduce damage and freezing effects, but will also increase prayer drain.

Nex smashes the floor, creating surround icicles that damage anyone caught next to her. Half of the icicles then being moving towards their assigned targets, hitting anyone caught in their way until the stop.

When Nex drops below <col=FFFFFF>20% life points</col> she will call on Glacies to aid her. Until this point, Glacies is invulnerable. If Glacies is killed, Nex will move onto the next stage, calling on the power of Zaros himself.

Nex calls on Zaros himself to empower her, This heals her, and increases her damage and accuracy for the remainder of her life. She will then cycle between using Soulsplit, Deflect Melee, and Leech curses against her opponents.

During the Zaros phase, Nex's melee attacks become area-of-effect, hitting anyone within 1 metre of her primary target.
When Nex is defeated, she'll activate the <col=FFFFFF>Wrath</col> curse, hitting anyone with an explosion who is nearby where she perishes.

During the fight, Nex can randomly decide to use a deflection curse <col=FFFFFF>(ranged or magic)</col> for <col=FFFFFF>2 minutes</col>. This becomes more probable as the phases carry on. She will only use one type per kill and will alternate between the two as kills go on.

The Queen Black Dragon cannot be defeated, only returned to slumber. To do this, you must activate <col=FFFFFF>four artefacts</col> that become enabled when the Queen Black Dragon reaches <col=FFFFFF>0 life points</col>.

The Queen Black Dragon will use a powerful swipe to any targets found at the front of her platform causing <col=FFFFFF>ranged</col> damage, if the target stands melee distance she will resort to biting them if they are completely adjacent.
The Queen Black Dragon can unleash massive fire breath at any point throughout the fight. Those who do not bring appropriate anti-fire protection will burn for incredible damage.

The Queen Black Dragon summons a massive wall of fire which passes over the platform inflicting fire damage. Keep an eye out for a weak point in the wall that you can pass through unharmed.

Based on the fights duration, the Queen Black Dragon may summon up to three walls of fire at the same time.

After the Queen Black Dragon has been defeated, you need to activate the next appropriate <col=FFFFFF>artefact</col>. While vulnerable, the queen will fire out <col=FFFFFF>grotworms</col> until the <col=FFFFFF>artefact</col> is enabled. These grotworms attack the player with magic, and they will stay until the rest of the fight.

From Stage two onwards, the Queen Black Dragon will spawn increasing amounts of Tortured souls. Tortured souls will fire arcane waves along the floor towards their target.

If they hit a different target on the way, they will disperse - otherwise they hit their target for unblockable damage.

A <col=FFFFFF>Tortured souls</col> may start chanting a ritual that will result in time stopping temporarily. If the spell completes, the target cannot move or act, but will suffer time stopping for <col=FFFFFF>10 seconds</col>, after which everything the Queen Black Dragon has done will be instantly applied.

Forging Fire is the ultimate fire breath attack the Queen Black Dragon will unleash in stage four. Any target standing in the centre of the fire will take massive fire damage. Note that this is enough heat to forge the royal crossbow.

Targets on the outskirts of the fire take less damage.
The Queen Black Dragon takes on the consistency of crystal. She is more resistant to magic, but weaker to physical damage for <col=FFFFFF>50 seconds, or until the next artefact is enabled.
The Queen Black Dragon hardens her carapace. She is more resistant to physical damage, but more vulnerable to magic for <col=FFFFFF>50 seconds, or until the next artefact is enabled.
TzTok-Jad has only one focus: killing his target. Expect to die if you do not protect against his massive melee attack. TzTok-Jad will only use melee swipe when the target gets within melee distance.
TzTok-Jad has only one focus: killing his target. Expect to die if you do not protect against his massive ranged attack.
TzTok-Jad has only one focus: killing his target. Expect to die if you do not protect against his massive magic attack.

When TzTok-Jad passes <col=FFFFFF>50% life points</col> he calls multiple Yt-HurKot's towards him, all with the aim of healing him. If kept unchecked, they will continually heal him for the duration of the encounter.
Vorago can only be defeated via use of the <col=FFFFFF>Maul of Omens</col>. This weapon can be assembled during the fight. Parts are found in <col=FFFFFF>stages 1, 2, and 4</col>.
Vorago hits his main target and swipes them for heavy melee damage. Having another tank in the vicinity can help lower the damage. Anyone adjacent to Vorago will also be hit.
The Magic Bomb is a magic attack that will attempt to target the furthest player away, multiple magic bombs will be fired at once should there be a large number of players fighting Vorago.

Vorago picks a target (preferring the farthest player away) and fires an explosive bomb towards them. On impact it detonates for significant damage - more so if multiple targets are in the explosive area.

At the end of each stage, Vorago will jump up and smash down in another location. Anyone caught in proximity to him landing risks taking heavy damage. After <col=FFFFFF>three smashes</col> the floor will give way and everyone will fall deeper into the encounter.

Vorago performs a strong melee attack against his main target five times in a row. Each attack will place a damage-over-time effect on the target, which persists if they are close to Vorago.

If the damage-over-time effect exists on Vorago's target when he attacks them again, the target will suffer a massive melee hit.

Using abilities such as Provoke and Freedom should be considered to deal with this attack.
Vorago picks a target and links himself to them for <col=FFFFFF>10 seconds</col>. During this time, any damage done to Vorago is instead applied to the linked target.

Vorago will spawn gravity fields in stage two. If a gravity field is activated and Vorago is nearby, it'll fly towards him. After Vorago has absorbed <col=FFFFFF>4 gravity fields (2 if players fail the next stage)</col> he will be destabilised and can be brought down.

After Vorago has absorbed <col=FFFFFF>4 gravity fields</col> all targets will become linked to Vorago and gravity itself. Opponents are then required to attack Vorago repeatedly to pull him into the floor, leaving him vulnerable.

After Vorago has been pulled into the floor, he will be idle and vulnerable for 10 seconds. During this time his opponents have to deal massive damage to obtain the piece of the Maul of Omens.

If this is failed, you are required to repeat the gravity fields once again.
Stage 3 is a special case. The chasm Vorago falls into may change week on week. Be prepared for any of the following!

Vorago will fire a projectile at the sky and follow it up. Shortly after a shadow will appear on the floor and the section of ceiling will fall down and smash anyone found underneath it. Slowly the entire arena may become blocked off if left unchecked.

If the arena is becoming locked down due to the <col=FFFFFF>ceiling collapse</col>, Vorago's opponents can choose to destroy the debris, but will take heavy damage in the process. Any leftover debris will also fall through into the next stage.

Scopuli are all tied to each other in spirit. The closer these creatures are to each other, the more accuracy and damage they will do, as well as increasing the distance they will inflict damage on their targets.
When a scopulus dies, it will heal its linked scopulus for <col=FFFFFF>10% of its life points</col> as well as enrage it - increasing its damage, accuracy, attack speed and attack spread.

Vorago will pick an area in the arena and fire a shockwave towards it. When the shockwave arrives, multiple <col=FFFFFF>vitalii</col> may spawn. To counteract this, you can have a person stand in the shockwave to prevent a <col=FFFFFF>vitalis</col> spawning, taking some damage instead.
Vitalii will attack anyone near to themselves or Vorago, hitting quickly for melee damage.

Vorago fires a green bomb at a random area in the encounter. On impact it will create a Gas cloud as well as bouncing towards a target. When it hits this target it will look to bounce again to another target.
Each unique target will take damage when it bounces to them.

If no targets are found, the bomb will explode immediately for massive damage.

If the bomb hits the same target twice it will detonate for heavy damage.
Standing in a gas cloud will drain run energy, <col=FFFFFF>adrenaline</col> and life points consistently.

Vorago will try to split the team in two. Half of the team will be marked as green and the other half red. Vorago also places coloured zones in the room and begins charging for <col=FFFFFF>8 seconds</col>.After this time, anyone not standing in the matching zone will explode for massive damage.

Vorago will open a waterfall from above and teleport to the centre of the encounter to begin charging. <col=FFFFFF>10 seconds later</col>, he will explode for massive fire damage. Anyone not hiding behind a waterfall will suffer massive damage from the fire.

Vorago will show some of his opponents stone versions of themselves. Each will have to defeat their stone clone, which will use a full suite of <col=FFFFFF>combat abilities</col>. If you defeat a clone, you may help team mates who also have stone clones.

In the final stage of the fight, opponents must face off against Vorago in a race of damage.

As Vorago inflicts damage, he will push his opponents west. If the team is pushed off of the platform, they all suffer instant death..

As the team damages Vorago, he will be pushed. east. If the team gets Vorago to the far end of the platform, he will be vulnerable to the Maul of Omens which can be used to finish him off.

extra.bslay_tactic_text: Solak will attempt to absorb anima from the grove by rooting his body into the ground. You must attack Solak's limbs and inflict enough damage on them to incapacitate him, causing his <col=FFFFFF>Blight-afflicted Core</col> to become exposed. The core must be defeated in order to proceed.

Solak causes a <col=FFFFFF>Blighted Anima Storm</col>, causing <col=FFFFFF>Blight Bombs</col> to periodically drop to the ground. The <col=FFFFFF>Anima Eruptions</col> must be destroyed in order to get closer to the <col=FFFFFF>Blighted Anima Storm</col> to dispel it.
Solak will cause multiple <col=FFFFFF>Blight Bombs</col> to rain down upon the arena. Carefully utilise <col=FFFFFF>Nature's Blessing</col> to survive this attack.

Solak will select a random player, stunning them and dragging them. He will smash one of his arms down onto the player and <col=FFFFFF>instantly kill</col> them if they do not escape. Solak unleashes this attack with such malice and force, his arm will become briefly stuck in the ground - the players may use this to their advantage.
Solak becomes engulfed in blight magic, overwhelming him and unleashing <col=FFFFFF>5</col> huge shockwaves that will strike every player in the arena for huge <col=FFFFFF>Blight</col> damage.

Roots will shoot up through the ground around Solak's current target, rapidly dealing <col=FFFFFF>Blight</col> damage to anyone standing on them. <col=FFFFFF>Blight Bombs</col> are also dropped onto other players, causing further roots to rapidly move between the afflicted players.

Merethiel will conjure 8 green sigils around the arena. When Solak is lured upon them, they will start to drain the corruption from within him.

Every time a sigil is filled with corruption, Merethiel will disable Solak, allowing you to enter Solak's Mind and defeat Erethdor.

Solak slams the ground with blight energy, causing all players to be rapidly struck with increasingly dangerous levels of <col=FFFFFF>Blight</col> damage. The only way to prevent Solak from continuously channelling the damage is to have enough players use <col=FFFFFF>stun abilities</col> on him.

extra.bslay_tactic_text:
Vorago raises his arms in the air and then slams them down, blocking off a corner of the room. Anyone outside of this area will begin to suffocate.

Vorago then moves his arms one by one 90 degrees anti-clockwise. In three of the corners he blocks you into there will be a bomb.

The magic and explosive bombs can be activated to drain one charge, firing that type of bomb at the player who activated it. The vitalis bomb can be activated to set it off, turning the team into explosive vitali.

At the end of his attack, Vorago will activate the vitalis bomb, if it has not been activated already, and fire the remaining explosive bombs at the team.

The third bomb reached during 'the end' will also be fired by Vorago in the later stages of the encounter. This bomb will turn you into a vitalis and home in on you for a number of seconds, exploding on impact to reduce adrenaline and deal damage to everyone nearby. On impact, the bomb will sap adrenaline from anyone it hits except for its main target. Use of the <col=E6DCB4>Barricade</col> ability could help to manage these bombs.

Before you can fight the Beastmaster, you must first endure several waves of aggressive foot soldiers.

The airut that enter the Pit of Trials are much more powerful than those you'll find anywhere else. They will attack with either ranged or melee, and have the potential to deal massive damage rapidly.

Unlike their brethren elsewhere, these airut require no Slayer knowledge to harm.
Chargers are vicious, dog-like creatures that are equipped with a spiked helmet. They will charge at their target and begin biting them with <col=FFFFFF>melee</col> attacks.

Midway through the ambush, Cormes will emerge from the western entrance of the arena. Cormes can attack from all three sides of the combat triangle. He will attack his target with either magic or ranged based on his target's defences.

Cormes' magic attack can inflict a burn; his ranged attack will drain run energy. Both attacks will hit any targets near his main target.

Cormes may also charge at a player, stunning them and hitting them for melee damage.

After surviving the initial onslaught, Beastmaster Durzag himself will enter the arena from the north. Along with him will be one of his pets, either Krar or Tuz.

The beastmaster will attack with melee and ranged. He will also have bombs, chargers, and cages at his disposal.
Durzag picks a target and throws a cage at them, preventing them from moving.
The beastmaster punches his target directly, dealing heavy <col=FFFFFF>melee</col> damage.

The beastmaster will slam his main target with a powerful punch. The smash is so powerful, it will deal melee damage to both players and monsters within <col=FFFFFF>2 squares</col> of himself or his target.
As the beastmaster attacks his main target, he will also launch spines that target those who are not under the attention of one of his pets, dealing ranged damage.

As the fight progresses, Durzag will grow enraged at his target. As his rage grows stronger, he will deal more damage and reset defensive abilities more often. The effect of his enrage can be countered with the <col=FFFFFF>Freedom</col> ability. Durzag also has a short attention span, and he will forget about his anger after some time if not focused on that target.
Durzag flails his arms wildly, dragging other targets in front of him and dealing melee damage to anyone caught in the attack.

Durzag will throw a bomb at a random target, these bombs will follow a player but can be avoided or disarmed. If not defused, it will explode for magic damage and reset the defensive abilities of anyone caught in the blast. The explosion is powerful, and it will hurt Durzag's beasts just as much as it hurts his targets.

Once one of his pets has been killed, Durzag will throw a bomb for every target.

Durzag drops several cages nearby, each containing a trapped charger. The cage containing the chargers can be opened by a teammate, otherwise they will all open at once on their own at 70%, attacking whoever set them free. If left imprisoned, they will break free themselves, and attack whomever they please.

When the fight begins, the cages that line the perimeter of the arena will also hold chargers. It is advised to free them yourself to have full control over whom they can attack.

Beastmaster Durzag has two pets that will help him in the fight. Both of Durzag's beasts have some shared attacks, but they still have their own methods of killing their target.

Durzag's first pet will enter the arena with him. His second pet will arrive when called, after his first beast is around 70% life points.

The beast will bite at their target, hitting anyone in the front of them for melee damage. If their target is up close, then the beasts will focus on biting them.

The bite can also open a flesh wound, increasing the damage that target takes from attacks. The wound can be partially healed with the Freedom ability, and it will slowly close itself over time; however, the beast may not let up, and continue to open the wound to prevent it from healing.
The beast will pounce at a target and begin to attack them with melee. When they pounce, they will also briefly stun the target.

If his target is out of biting distance, Krar will fling spines at them and anyone nearby.

These spines deal heavy ranged damage and will also drain the target's run energy. If his target is out of energy, his attacks will stun them instead.

If his target is out of biting distance, Tuz will blast magic at them and anyone nearby.

The attack also inflicts a magical burn that deals further damage regularly.

The burn can be removed with the Freedom ability, but Tuz will quickly attempt to apply another.

The closer his beasts are to him, the more accurate Durzag's attacks are. Keep his pets at a distance to minimise the damage you take.

Should the pets die he Durzag will inherit the on-hit ability of his pets (except Cormes).

Once the beastmaster has been lowered to 50% of his life points, he will become significantly enraged, increasing the strength and frequency of his attacks.

If either of his pets are still alive, Durzag will take significantly less damage until they are defeated.

Gongs are hung at the centre of each of the four walls. The loud ring of the gong will disrupt Durzag's only reliable sense: his hearing.

Ringing a gong will cost some prayer points, but the result will be effective in confusing Durzag.

If successful, the gong will completely drain the prayer points of whoever rang it, but the noise will halve the beastmaster's attack speed. The gongs are heavy and fragile, so each one can only be used to discombobulate Durzag once.

Goebies are cute, rocky creatures that have been held captive by the Beastmaster. Goebies will attempt to assist you in the fight, but they have been left in a weakened state from their imprisonment.

The evil beasts that held them captive will target the goebies just as much as they target you.

It is best if they are focused on you, so provoke any charger or airut that plans to harm one of the little fellows. Remember that freeing the goebies is the goal of this raid; their safety is second to none!

Yakamaru's attacks are fuelled by the power of water. As he attacks his main target, he will slowly soak them with water, increasing the power of his attacks. Any one close to his main target will also experience the effects of his drench. The only way to counter this is by using <col=FFFFFF>Freedom</col> to shake some of the water off.
Players who completely avoid all combat with Yakamaru will enrage him, prompting him to fling projectiles at those he considers cowards in an attempt to lure them into combat.
Yakamaru splashes the floor, damaging anyone within <col=FFFFFF>2 squares</col> of him with a powerful <col=FFFFFF>magic</col> attack.

Yakamaru summons small tendrils to pierce anyone outside of his splash distance. These tendrils will always hit his main target and those nearby, but they will not target anyone else preoccupied with another fight.

Yakamaru picks a target and soaks them to the fullest extent, turning them into an entity of pure water. Whoever has this form will gradually take increased damage from it. The effect can be passed between teammates by standing together to avoid damage. After a few passes, the soaked form will dissipate completely.

Yakamaru spits a <col=FFFFFF>jellyfish</col> out at the team. When it lands, it will create <col=FFFFFF>5 geysers</col> linked to it. Each geyser can be stood on to remove <col=FFFFFF>20%</col> of the jellyfish's life points, but they will also deal <col=FFFFFF>magic</col> damage to anyone on top when they erupt.
Jellyfish are powerful creatures that choose a target and barrage them with attacks. Their attack deals melee damage to anyone in a <col=FFFFFF>3x3</col> area of their main target.
The fight will begin in the central pool. In this pool, Yakamaru can use his <col=FFFFFF>Soak</col> and <col=FFFFFF>Jelly spawn</col> special attacks.

As the fight progresses, Yakamaru will swap pools, giving him new techniques in combat. Yakamaru will choose the first outside pool at <col=FFFFFF>random</col> and will continue from there <col=FFFFFF>clockwise</col> as the fight goes on.
In the southernmost pool, Yakamaru has access to much more powerful tendrils. In this pool, he can use his <col=FFFFFF>Soak, Jelly spawn,</col> and <col=FFFFFF>Tendril assault</col> special attacks.
Yakamaru assaults the team with two different tendril attacks simultaneously — <col=FFFFFF>Strangling tendrils</col> and <col=FFFFFF>Whipping tendrils.</col>

Strangling tendrils target the players whom Yakamaru considers the most dangerous. These tendrils latch onto the <col=FFFFFF>top five damage dealers</col>, preventing movement and resetting all defensive abilities. They asphyxiate their target, dealing gradually increased damage. The only way to escape is to fight back; you must deal enough damage back at Yakamaru for the choking to stop.

Yakamaru goes full assault against his current target, summoning a large tendril growth that whips around wildly. Anyone caught inside this growth will take massive damage rapidly, unless they are being asphyxiated by the <col=FFFFFF>strangling tendrils</col>.

In the south-west pool, Yakamaru calls on creatures of the sea to assist in the fight. In this pool, he can use his <col=FFFFFF>Soak, Jelly spawn,</col> and <col=FFFFFF>Sharknado</col> special attacks.

Yakamaru begins whirling a cyclone, pulling up dangerous explosive fish. While the cyclone is still charging, the sharks can be fished out, removing one explosive charge from the attack.

Any charges remaining will be launched at the team. Yakamaru will attempt to home one fish to each combatant, randomly scattering any spares. When the fish land, they will explode after a few seconds. Fish them away or just run to avoid taking heavy damage.

In the north-west pool, Yakamaru will make use of his environment to attack his targets. In this pool, he can use his <col=FFFFFF>Soak, Jelly spawn,</col> and <col=FFFFFF>Quicksand</col> special attacks.

Yakamaru dampens the ground, leaving <col=FFFFFF>two</col> targets standing. Everyone else will be trapped in quicksand, and slowly sink to the bottom. Anyone with mobility will need to <col=FFFFFF>free</col> their teammates. Anyone who sinks below the ground will suffer <col=FFFFFF>instant death</col>.

In the northernmost pool Yakamaru can use his Soak and Jelly spawn special attacks.

The longer Yakamaru sits in this pool, the harder his body becomes. In his weakest state, Yakamaru will take increased damage, but as his body hardens, he will take less and less damage. To reset his defences, he must be stunned with an ability. When stunned, Yakamaru will immediately retaliate, damaging every target; the weaker Yakamaru is when he is stunned, the more damage he will deal when he retaliates.

Near the end of each pool, Yakamaru will purge a poison from his body. To properly defeat the pool, someone will need to absorb the poison and bring it to Yakamaru. If a poisoned player is within splash distance, Yakamaru will be enticed by the scent of the poison and swallow the player whole when defeated.

When the poison transfers to Yakamaru, he will return to the central pool, regurgitating the player he swallowed. The regurgitated player will drown and wash ashore, along with 5 planks that will be needed for later. When Yakamaru returns to the central pool, he will also spawn a Jelly group to come to his aid.

The player who was swallowed and regurgitated by Yakamaru will wash ashore incapacitated. One of their teammates will need to perform CPR before the drowning victim loses breath. If not saved, drowning will cause <col=FFFFFF>instant death.</col>
When Yakamaru is still inflicted with the poison he absorbed, he will take increased damage from all attacks.

As Yakamaru returns to the central pool, <col=FFFFFF>four jellyfish</col> will spawn and begin moving towards Yakamaru. There is one jellyfish for each side of the combat triangle - <col=FFFFFF>meleefish, magical jellyfish, piercing jellyfish</col> - and one support jellyfish. If any of these jellyfish reach Yakamaru, they will absorb the poison from his body, curing him. If either of the support jellyfish dies, their death will cure Yakamaru.
Durable jellyfish can attack with magic, but their main focus will be <col=FFFFFF>healing</col> Yakamaru and other jelly fish.

While the reflecting jellyfish is alive, the three jellyfish in its group will take decreased damage, with <col=FFFFFF>1/4</col> of that damage being dealt back to players. Reflecting jellyfish are also immune to regular attacks. Each jellyfish under the reflecting jellyfish's protection will damage the reflecting jellyfish for <col=FFFFFF>1/3</col> of its maximum life points when it dies.

Once Yakamaru has been defeated in every pool, he will hide away and create four images of himself, one in each outer pool. These images do not have as many life points as the real Yakamaru, but they are just as powerful offensively. All four images will need to be fought at once; any image that is not in combat will <col=FFFFFF>fling projectiles</col> at the team for increasingly heavy damage.

Unlike the real Yakamaru, mirage images will not return to the central pool when defeated. Instead, they will leap into the air to regenerate their life points. While this is happening, the team will have <col=FFFFFF>5 seconds</col> to block the pool. If not blocked, the image will respawn with full life points and continue attacking. The <col=FFFFFF>southernmost</col> and <col=FFFFFF>north-west</col> pools require <col=FFFFFF>10 piles of sand</col> from the area to be blocked. The <col=FFFFFF>south-west</col> and <col=FFFFFF>northernmost</col> pools require <col=FFFFFF>10 reclaimed planks</col> to be blocked.
After the final image has been defeated, Yakamaru will emerge from the central pool one final time. Once the last bits of his health are taken away, Yakamaru will collapse, defeated.

extra.bslay_tactic_text: Representing Zaros as General, the deadly duo of Vindicta & Gorvek await any players who step forward.
If Vindicta is unable to attack the player she will use her ranged attack.
After a few attacks and raising her sword in the air, Vindicta will call on Gorvek to unleash dragonfire on her target, dealing rapid magic damage.
Upon dropping to a certain amount of lifepoints Vindicta will mount Gorvek, during this time a mix of melee and ranged attacks follow.
Once the melee and ranged attacks have finished, Gorvek comes down from above and leaves a trail of dragonfire.

In Hard Mode, Vindicta and Gorvek have a combined total of 600,000 lifepoints making them a formidable boss to take on. During Hard Mode they will also attack faster resulting in higher damage per second.
One half of the Twin Furies, Avaryss focuses on <col=FFFFFF>melee</col> attacks towards the player.

Avarays lines up to start a surge attack towards the player. She will charge four times, each time from a different corner of the arena. Players caught in her path will be slammed into the wall by her, taking <col=FFFFFF>melee</col> damage.

extra.bslay_tactic_text: Nymora begins to charge up a special attack, during this time spikes will fall from the ceiling covering the entire arena except for the area Nymora is in.
The Arena around the Twin Furies will be engulfed in flames as they link up and begin to charge up a highly explosive attack, during this time the Twin Furies are more vulnerable to attacks.
As the Burn Phase is ongoing, a bar will start to degrade above the Twin Furies heads, once depleted the Furies will emit a huge and powerful explosion.

A Lava Bomb will bounce around the arena, dealing large damage to anything it touches and exploding on the last bounce, keep an eye out for a green marker which informs you where the Lava Bomb will land.

At times a Blue Lava Bomb will appear in the arena, this has a different effect to the normal Lava Bombs, if the player stands underneath the Blue Bomb as it hits them it will reflect on to the Twin Furies dealing damage to them.

However, if the player is unable to reflect the Blue Bomb back to the Twin Furies after a few attempts the Blue Bomb will lock on to a player and deal high damage.
A general of Seren's army, Helwyr uses elven magic to draw upon the energy of the creature he possesses.
During the fight Helywr may call upon nature to help him out, at this moment three gas-puffing mushrooms appear (six if you're in Hard mode) and will deal damage if you are near them.
Helwyr uses his claws to rake an area in front of him dealing bleed damage to you if you're hit by it.
When Rend is in effect any attack Helwyr strikes with will cause bleed damage, the bleed effect will stack on top of Rake.
Helwyr pounces a random player and thrashes around, biting and clawing everything around
Helwyr calls in a pack of Cywir Alphas, these deal quick damage and should be killed quickly to avoid losing life.
Gregorovic is the general of Sliske's army, possessing accurate and high-damage attacks.
Using his glaives, Gregorovic can utilize <col=FFFFFF>melee</col> and <col=FFFFFF>ranged</col> attacks, Gregorovic is also capable of poisoning the player in quick intervals.

Gregorovic summons a Spirit of Rage, Spirit of Delirium or Spirit of Mania from the respective masks depending on where Gregorovic is positioned when he uses that ability, if you're fighting Gregorovic in Hard Mode two spirits will be spawned instead of one.

Gregorovic will toss both of his glaives into the air, shadows will appear throughout the arena in a scattered formation. After two seconds, daggers and knives will fall from the ceiling and deal magic damage onto the player.

Upon reaching a certain threshold of lifepoints, Gregorovic will summon 2/3 shadows, these shadows have a small amount of lifepoints, while the shadows are alive Gregorovic can swap places with the shadow copies.
Telos awakens, and begins the fight with 4 main abilities.

A green beam of anima will appear across the platform. Standing inside the beam will increase adrenaline gain, whilst draining prayer points. Telos' anima will increase faster if it is standing in the beam.
Telos will channel a tendril attack which drains adrenaline. Whilst the tendril is being channeled, Telos will both heal, and rapidly gain anima. The channel can be broken by dealing damage.
Telos will deal <col=FFFFFF>melee</col> damage that stuns the target, followed up by a jump dealing typeless damage.
Telos will charge his sword with energy, and perform a slice dealing high typeless damage.

extra.bslay_tactic_text: Upon entering phase two, Telos gains the ability to use onslaught. Alongside this, the beam is now corrupt.
A black beam of anima will appear across the platform. Standing inside the beam will reduce all damage taken & damage dealt. This has the same effect on Telos if stood inside the beam.
Telos begins channelling onslaught,which is a magic attack with each consecutive hit becoming stronger. This ability continues until Telos is drained of anima.
Telos attacks primarily with <col=FFFFFF>magic</col>, and gains two additional abilities depending on its anima. Minions will also be charging Telos with anima.
Three charging minions will be active, charging Telos with anima. They can be brought to 0 health to prevent them from charging Telos, however will regenerate after a short period of time.
If Telos' anima is in the lower red section of the bar, It will periodically drain your adrenaline.
If Telos' anima is in the higher red section of the bar, it periodically causes explosions, dealing high amounts of damage.
Telos attacks primarily with <col=FFFFFF>melee</col>, however will begin to use <col=FFFFFF>magic</col> if out of range.
Telos gains the ability to summon three minions when reaching a certain percentage of health remaining. All of the summoned minions will deal <col=FFFFFF>melee</col> damage.
Pure golems deal significantly more damage than the others.
Corrupt golems add the break armour stacking debuff, reducing the targets armour by 1% per stack.
Volcanic golems have the ability to stun and bind their target.

extra.task_step_1: You can buy <col=0xF0BE79>beer</col> from a <col=0xF0BE79>bartender</col> in <col=0xF0BE79>Varrock</col> or <col=0xF0BE79>Port Sarim</col> for 2 coins.
extra.task_step_2: <col=0xF0BE79>Drink</col> the <col=0xF0BE79>beer</col> in your <col=0xF0BE79>backpack</col>.
extra.task_information: Drinking beer will temporarily increase your Strength and decrease your Attack. There are rarer sorts of beer that have different effects.
extra.cheevo_details: Drink a cheap beer.

extra.task_step_1: Talk to <col=0xF0BE79>Xuan</col> in <col=0xF0BE79>Varrock</col> or <col=0xF0BE79>Burthorpe</col> and browse the Loyalty Programme rewards in his shop.
extra.task_information:
You gain more loyalty points the longer you are a member.
You can spend these points to get exciting emotes and auras to help you throughout your adventures!
extra.cheevo_details: Learn about the Loyalty Shop.

extra.task_step_1: The <col=0xF0BE79>Grand Exchange</col> is located in the <col=0xF0BE79>north-west</col> of <col=0xF0BE79>Varrock</col>.
extra.task_information:
It is a good place to buy and sell items in bulk.
The Grand Exchange value of items is determined by player supply and demand, so you'll usually get better prices than selling to shops.
extra.cheevo_details: Visit the Grand Exchange.

extra.potion_info_custom_text: For the next <col=0x00ffff>4 hammer swings</col>, your <col=0x00ffff>smithing progress</col> is multiplied by <col=0x00ff00>10</col>.

extra.task_information: Remember if you are using a crossbow that they fire bolts rather than arrows. You can wear a shield while wielding a crossbow for extra defence.
extra.cheevo_details: Equip a shortbow, longbow and crossbow, in any order.

extra.task_step_1: You will need 2 <col=0xF0BE79>bronze bars</col> to make this weapon.
extra.task_step_2: You can mine <col=0xF0BE79>tin</col> and <col=0xF0BE79>copper</col> ore to smelt into a bronze bar at a <col=0xF0BE79>furnace</col>.
extra.task_step_3: Smith the bar into a <col=0xF0BE79>bronze mace</col> at an <col=0xF0BE79>anvil</col>.
extra.task_information:
Maces do crushing damage.
Some monsters are more vulnerable to crushing than stabbing or slashing.
extra.cheevo_details: Make a bronze mace of your own.

extra.task_step_1: You need <col=0xF0BE79>level 3 Magic</col> to cast this spell.
extra.task_step_2: You will also need 1 <col=0xF0BE79>mind rune</col>. The magic shop in Varrock sells these.
extra.task_step_3: Open your <col=0xF0BE79>Magic Spellbook</col> and locate the <col=0xF0BE79>Confuse</col> combat spell.
extra.task_step_4: <col=0xF0BE79>Left-click</col> the <col=0xF0BE79>Confuse</col> spell and target an <col=0xF0BE79>attackable enemy</col>.
extra.task_rewards: Completing this achievement will give an amount of money based on total achievements completed, a sapphire necklace and ten cosmic runes.
extra.cheevo_details: Successfully cast the Confuse spell.
extra.task_step_4_mobile: <col=0xF0BE79>Tap</col> the <col=0xF0BE79>Confuse</col> spell and target an <col=0xF0BE79>attackable enemy</col>.

extra.task_step_1: You will need level <col=0xF0BE79>5 Fishing</col> and <col=0xF0BE79>fishing bait</col> to catch sardines. The fishing shop in Lumbridge sells these.
extra.task_step_2: Go to a saltwater fishing spot, such as the shore east of Lumbridge swamp.
extra.task_step_3: <col=0xF0BE79>Right-click</col> a net <col=0xF0BE79>fishing spot</col>, and choose <col=0xF0BE79>Bait</col>. You'll start using the fishing rod on your tool belt.
extra.task_rewards: Completing this achievement will give an amount of money based on total achievements completed, and five raw herring.
extra.task_information:
Fish are the staple of an adventurer's diet.
If you're planning to catch a lot of fish, be sure to bring plenty of fishing bait. Each fish you catch will consume bait.
At level 10 Fishing, you are able to fish herring when fishing with bait.
extra.cheevo_details: Catch some sardines.
extra.task_step_3_mobile: <col=0xF0BE79>Long-press</col> a net <col=0xF0BE79>fishing spot</col>, and choose <col=0xF0BE79>Bait</col>. You'll start using the fishing rod on your tool belt.

extra.task_step_1: Acquire a raw herring by fishing or by buying it.
extra.task_step_2: To fish for herring, use a rod and bait at a saltwater bait fishing spot with at least <col=0xF0BE79>10 Fishing</col>.
extra.task_step_3: Use your <col=0xF0BE79>raw herring</col> on a <col=0xF0BE79>range</col> or <col=0xF0BE79>fire</col> with at least <col=0xF0BE79>5 Cooking</col>.
extra.task_step_4: It is possible to burn your herring by mistake, so you may wish to bring several.
extra.cheevo_details: Cook a herring.

extra.task_step_1: You will need level <col=0xF0BE79>7 Magic</col> to cast this spell.
extra.task_step_2: You will also need a 1 <col=0xF0BE79>water rune</col> and 1 <col=0xF0BE79>cosmic rune</col>, and an item of <col=0xF0BE79>sapphire jewellery</col> to cast it on.
extra.task_step_3: The magic shop in Varrock sells water runes.
extra.task_step_4: Completing the achievement <col=0xF0BE79>Not So Confusing After All</col> will allow you to claim a <col=0xF0BE79>sapphire amulet</col> and a <col=0xF0BE79>cosmic rune</col> from <col=0xF0BE79>Explorer Jack</col> in <col=0xF0BE79>Lumbridge</col>, or any other taskmaster.
extra.task_step_5: Open your <col=0xF0BE79>Magic Spellbook</col> and locate the <col=0xF0BE79>Lvl-1 Enchant</col> skilling spell.
extra.task_step_6: <col=0xF0BE79>Left-click</col> <col=0xF0BE79>Lvl-1 Enchant</col>, then <col=0xF0BE79>left-click</col> the <col=0xF0BE79>jewellery</col> you wish to enchant.
extra.task_step_7: Free players can only enchant amulets.
extra.task_information: Enchanted jewellery has a wide range of effects including teleports, smelting assistance, damage reflection in combat and even improved luck.
extra.cheevo_details: Successfully cast Level-1 Enchant on an item of jewellery.
extra.task_step_6_mobile: <col=0xF0BE79>Tap</col> <col=0xF0BE79>Lvl-1 Enchant</col>, then <col=0xF0BE79>tap</col> the <col=0xF0BE79>jewellery</col> you wish to enchant.

extra.potion_info_custom_text: Temporarily <col=0x00ff00>doubles</col> your current <col=0x00ffff>lifepoints</col>.

extra.task_step_1: You will need <col=0xF0BE79>10 Ranged</col> to wield an oak bow.
extra.task_step_2: You can buy one from <col=0xF0BE79>Lowe</col>'s Archery Emporium in <col=0xF0BE79>Varrock</col>.
extra.task_information: Higher level shortbows are more accurate; longbows sacrifice speed for even more accuracy.
extra.cheevo_details: Equip an oak shortbow or longbow.

extra.task_step_1: You may buy <col=0xF0BE79>iron arrows</col> at <col=0xF0BE79>Lowe</col>'s Archery Emporium in <col=0xF0BE79>Varrock</col>, or you can fletch them yourself with <col=0xF0BE79>iron arrowheads</col> (smithed from <col=0xF0BE79>iron bars</col> with level <col=0xF0BE79>20 Smithing</col>), and <col=0xF0BE79>headless arrows</col> (from <col=0xF0BE79>arrow shafts</col> and <col=0xF0BE79>feathers</col> with level <col=0xF0BE79>15 Fletching</col>).
extra.task_information: The tips of the arrows you equip have an effect on the damage you can do with your shots.
extra.cheevo_details: Equip iron arrows in your ammunition slot.

extra.task_information: Iron weapons are both more accurate and more damaging than bronze.
extra.cheevo_name: Not What We Mean By Irony
extra.cheevo_details: Wield a melee weapon made of iron.

extra.task_information: Armour made out of stronger metals will protect you better. Iron is stronger than bronze but weaker than steel.
extra.cheevo_name: All's Ferrous in Love and War
extra.cheevo_details: Wear a piece of armour made of iron.

extra.task_step_1: You will need level <col=0xF0BE79>10 Cooking</col>.

extra.task_step_3: Use the <col=0xF0BE79>pastry dough</col> with a <col=0xF0BE79>pie dish</col> to make a pie shell - Beefy Bill near Lumbridge Mill can sell you a pie dish.
extra.task_step_4: Fill the <col=0xF0BE79>pie shell</col> with <col=0xF0BE79>redberries</col> (you can find some on bushes south of Varrock's south-east wall).
extra.task_step_5: Cook the <col=0xF0BE79>redberry pie</col> on a <col=0xF0BE79>range</col> or stove.
extra.cheevo_details: Bake a redberry pie.

extra.task_information: Steel weapons are stronger than iron or bronze.
extra.cheevo_details: Wield a weapon made of steel.

extra.task_information: Steel armour is between iron and mithril in effectiveness.

extra.task_step_2: Climb the <col=0xF0BE79>stairs</col> to the upper flour of the mill, and put the <col=0xF0BE79>wheat</col> in the <col=0xF0BE79>hopper</col>.

extra.task_step_1: Get <col=0xF0BE79>air runes</col> by <col=0xF0BE79>runecrafting</col> at the <col=0xF0BE79>air altar</col>, or <col=0xF0BE79>trade with Apprentice Clara</col> in the <col=0xF0BE79>Burthorpe</col> Runecrafting shop.
extra.task_step_2: Get a <col=0xF0BE79>staff</col>. (Defeating Caitlin during the <col=0xF0BE79>Blood Pact quest</col> will drop her staff for you.)
extra.task_step_3: Get magic armour, such as a <col=0xF0BE79>wizard hat</col>, <col=0xF0BE79>wizard robes</col> or <col=0xF0BE79>spellstorm drape</col>. (You can defeat enemies (such as <col=0xF0BE79>white wolves</col> and <col=0xF0BE79>trolls</col> in <col=0xF0BE79>Burthorpe</col>, or <col=0xF0BE79>spellwisps</col> outside the <col=0xF0BE79>Wizards' Tower</col>, or purchase it from the <col=0xF0BE79>Grand Exchange</col> or <col=0xF0BE79>Thessalia's Fine Clothes</col> in <col=0xF0BE79>Varrock</col>.)
extra.task_step_4: Open your <col=0xF0BE79>backpack</col> by left-clicking the helmet/satchel icon on your ribbon menu.
extra.task_step_5: Left-click any <col=0xF0BE79>magic armour</col> in your <col=0xF0BE79>backpack</col> to wear it.
extra.task_step_6: Left-click the <col=0xF0BE79>staff</col> in your <col=0xF0BE79>backpack</col> to wield it.
extra.task_information:
Some staves provide an infinite supply of a rune needed to cast certain spells.
eg Caitlyn's staff gives you unlimited air runes, and a mindspike or staff of fire gives unlimited fire runes.
extra.cheevo_details: Equip a staff while wearing magic armour, with air runes in your backpack.

extra.task_step_1: To cast <col=0xF0BE79>Air Strike</col>, you will need to wield a magic weapon and <col=0xF0BE79>air runes</col>. (You can <col=0xF0BE79>trade with Apprentice Clara</col> in the <col=0xF0BE79>Burthorpe</col> Runecrafting shop to get limited free runes, or runecraft them yourself.)
extra.task_step_2: Open your <col=0xF0BE79>(Combat) Magic Spellbook</col> and left-click the <col=0xF0BE79>Air Strike</col> icon to set it as your auto-cast spell.
extra.task_step_3: <col=0xF0BE79>Attack</col> a suitable target to cast the spell at it.
extra.task_step_4: You can keep using the spell as your attack as long as you have runes.
extra.task_information:
Air Strike is your first attack spell; as you gain levels in Magic you can unlock more powerful variants.
As you increase your Magic level, you will unlock access to new spells and abilities, such as Confuse, enchanting, teleports, and alchemy.
extra.cheevo_details: Cast Air Strike at a dummy or a hostile target.

extra.task_step_1: <col=0xF0BE79>Talk to Bryll Thoksdottir</col> at the <col=0xF0BE79>Taverley pier</col> to sail to the <col=0xF0BE79>Daemonheim</col> peninsula.
extra.task_step_2: Head north-west to the entrance to Daemonheim, and claim a <col=0xF0BE79>Ring of Kinship</col> from the <col=0xF0BE79>Dungeoneering tutor</col>.
extra.task_step_3: <col=0xF0BE79>Right-click</col> the <col=0xF0BE79>Ring of Kinship</col> in your <col=0xF0BE79>backpack</col> and choose <col=0xF0BE79>Teleport to Daemonheim</col>.
extra.task_information:
Delve into the depths of the dungeon of Daemonheim. Fight monsters, collect keys, unlock doors, solve puzzles, defeat bosses, and use all the skills at your disposal, either alone or with your friends.
You gain experience in the Dungeoneering skill each time you complete a Daemonheim floor.
extra.cheevo_details: Teleport to Daemonheim with a Ring of Kinship.
extra.task_step_3_mobile: <col=0xF0BE79>Long-press</col> the <col=0xF0BE79>Ring of Kinship</col> in your <col=0xF0BE79>backpack</col> and choose <col=0xF0BE79>Teleport to Daemonheim</col>.

extra.task_step_1: Claim a Ring of Kinship if you have not already.
extra.task_step_2: Ensure you're near the entrance to Daemonheim.
extra.task_step_3: <col=0xF0BE79>Right-click</col> the <col=0xF0BE79>Ring of Kinship</col> and choose <col=0xF0BE79>Open Party Interface</col>.
extra.task_step_4: On the party interface, left-click <col=0xF0BE79>Form Party</col> to start a Dungeoneering group.
extra.task_information:
Once you have a party, you can raid floors of the Daemonheim dungeons to earn Dungeoneering experience and tokens.
You can invite up to four additional players to join your party, or delve into Daemonheim alone.
extra.cheevo_details: Form a Dungeoneering party.
extra.task_step_3_mobile: <col=0xF0BE79>Long-press</col> the <col=0xF0BE79>Ring of Kinship</col> and choose <col=0xF0BE79>Open Party Interface</col>.
extra.task_step_4_mobile: On the party interface, tap <col=0xF0BE79>Form Party</col> to start a Dungeoneering group.

extra.task_step_1: Form a Dungeoneering party (see the <col=0xF0BE79>Party On, Dudes</col> achievement).
extra.task_step_2: Daemonheim provides its own equipment. If you are carrying items that cannot be taken into Daemonheim, deposit them at the Fremennik banker.
extra.task_step_3: Left-click the <col=0xF0BE79>dungeon entrance</col>, choose the level and complexity to raid, and <col=0xF0BE79>enter the dungeon</col>!
extra.task_step_4: Navigate the dungeon using all your skills, defeat the boss, and proceed to the next floor.
extra.task_information:
Increasing your Dungeoneering level opens more floors of Daemonheim and allows access to secret resource dungeons in the rest of Gielinor.
Dungeoneering tokens can be traded for powerful items and abilities.
extra.cheevo_details: Complete a Dungeoneering floor.

extra.task_step_1: Obtain <col=0xF0BE79>1,000 coins</col> by any means necessary.
extra.task_step_2: Visit <col=0xF0BE79>Alfred Stonemason</col>, the Construction tutor in <col=0xF0BE79>Rimmington</col> (or the estate agent in Ardougne, Varrock or Falador).
extra.task_step_3: Ask the estate agent how you can get your very own house, and buy it.
extra.task_information: Once you have a plot of your own, you can start building a customised house on it.
extra.cheevo_details: Buy a house of your own.

extra.task_step_1: You need at least <col=0xF0BE79>5,000 coins</col> to build a kitchen.
extra.task_step_2: A kitchen requires <col=0xF0BE79>level 5 Construction</col>. You can increase your Construction level by building furniture in your parlour and garden.
extra.task_step_3: Visit your house in <col=0xF0BE79>Building Mode</col> via the <col=0xF0BE79>house portal</col>.
extra.task_step_4: <col=0xF0BE79>Right-click</col> any <col=0xF0BE79>door hotspot</col> and choose to <col=0xF0BE79>build</col> a <col=0xF0BE79>kitchen</col>.
extra.task_step_5: Rotate the room to your satisfaction and confirm your purchase to build it.
extra.task_information: You can personalise a room you have built with furniture and fixtures.
extra.cheevo_details: Build a room in your house (such as a kitchen).
extra.task_step_4_mobile: <col=0xF0BE79>Long-press</col> any <col=0xF0BE79>door hotspot</col> and choose to <col=0xF0BE79>build</col> a <col=0xF0BE79>kitchen</col>.
