extra.task_step_1: Travel to a location where wisps gather. The first of these locations can be found to the west of Lumbridge.
extra.task_step_2: Click on a wisp to transform it into a spring and gather memories.
extra.task_information: Collected memories can be taken to one of the craters located near wisp colonies. Here, you can convert the memories into experience or energy.
extra.cheevo_details: Gather a memory of any tier.
extra.task_step_2_mobile: Tap a wisp to transform it into a spring and gather memories.

extra.task_step_1: Take a memory, or an enriched memory, to one of the craters located near wisp colonies.
extra.task_step_2: Click on the crater and your memories will be turned into experience.
extra.task_information: Memories can be collected from the wisps in each colony. Multiple memories of any tier can be converted at the same time, and higher tier memories will give a larger amount of experience when converted.
extra.cheevo_details: Convert a memory, or an enriched memory, into experience.
extra.task_step_2_mobile: Tap the crater and your memories will be turned into experience.

extra.task_step_1: Take a memory, or an enriched memory, to one of the craters located near wisp colonies.
extra.task_step_2: Right-click on the crater and configure,then choose to convert your memory into energy. Now whenever you click on the crater, it will turn any memories into energy instead of experience.
extra.task_information: Memories can be collected from the wisps in each colony. Multiple memories of any tier can be converted at the same time, and higher tier memories will give a larger amount of energy when converted.
extra.cheevo_details: Convert a memory, or an enriched memory, into energy.
extra.task_step_2_mobile: Long-press the crater and configure,then choose to convert your memory into energy. Now whenever you tap the crater, it will turn any memories into energy instead of experience.

extra.task_step_1: You will need a memory, or an enriched memory, along with some energy of the same tier.
extra.task_step_2: Take your memory and energy to one of the craters located near wisp colonies.
extra.task_information: Converting memories into enhanced experience gives a greater amount of experience. However, it also uses up some energy. Converting normal memories requires 5 energy of the same tier per conversion, while enriched memories require 10 energy. Multiple memories of any tier can be converted at the same time, and higher tier memories will give a larger amount of experience when converted.
extra.cheevo_details: Convert a memory, or an enriched memory, into enhanced experience.

extra.task_step_1: Get some energy of the appropriate tier and additional materials as described in the Divination section of the skill guide.
extra.task_step_2: Click on the energy and choose a portent to create.
extra.task_step_3: Creating portents has various requirements. As you get more proficient, you can create higher-level items.
extra.task_information: Most portents will sit passively in your inventory until they are required. For example, portents of restoration will only activate when you fall below half health. Experiment with different types of portent to discover their uses.
extra.cheevo_details: Create a portent.
extra.task_step_2_mobile: Tap the energy and choose a portent to create.

extra.task_step_1: Get some energy of the appropriate tier and additional materials as described in the Divination section of the skill guide.
extra.task_step_2: Click on the energy and choose a divine location to create.
extra.task_step_3: Creating divine locations has various requirements. As you become more proficient, you can create higher-level items.
extra.task_information: You may only craft one divine location per day. When you have crafted a location, you can place it on the ground and - if you have the required skills - gather from it. Any other player with the required skills can also interact with the location. When other players interact with a location you placed, you have a chance to gain noted versions of the items they collect.
extra.cheevo_details: Create a divine location.
extra.task_step_2_mobile: Tap the energy and choose a divine location to create.

extra.task_step_1: Get some energy of the appropriate tier and additional materials as described in the Divination section of the skill guide.
extra.task_step_2: Click on the energy and choose a sign to create.
extra.task_step_3: Creating signs has various requirements. As you get more proficient you can create higher-level items.
extra.task_information: Most signs must be equipped to take effect. When equipped, the signs will sit passively until they are required. For example, the sign of life will only activate on death. Experiment with different types of sign to discover their uses.
extra.cheevo_details: Create a sign.
extra.task_step_2_mobile: Tap the energy and choose a sign to create.

extra.task_step_1: Get some energy of the appropriate tier as described in the Divination section of the skill guide.
extra.task_step_2: Click on the energy and choose a boon to unlock.
extra.task_step_3: Different boons have different requirements to create. As you get more proficient you can unlock higher level boons.
extra.task_information: Unlocking a boon means you will get a 10% higher yield for both energy and experience for that tier. For example, the flickering boon means you will gain 10% more energy or 10% more XP when converting flickering memories. You may only unlock a boon once, as its effects are permanent.
extra.cheevo_details: Unlock a boon.
extra.task_step_2_mobile: Tap the energy and choose a boon to unlock.

extra.bslay_tactic_text: A mysterious figure, he is located at the Crossing between life and death. He uses an obelisk to harness the power of souls and has a particular interest in the World Guardian's soul.
The Magister launches a highly accurate, powerful ranged attack at his opponent.

If the Magister is close to his target, he will strike them with his staff, stunning them, before teleporting away. Alternatively, if he is at a distance, he will close the gap and strike his target; if they are not praying melee, their prayers will drop.

The Magister throws an unstable mixture at his target. After between 2.4 - 4.8 seconds the mixture explodes, dealing damage to all within range. The mixture can be kicked back at the Magister, dealing damage if it hits him.
Two imperial akh are summoned from the grave to assist the Magister in defeating his target - these may be either a warrior, mage or ranger.
The Magister begins to drain his target's health, healing for the same amount. This attack can be interrupted by running out of range or using a melee threshold or ultimate ability against him.

The Magister activates the soul obelisk which then begins to drain your soul, which lowers your Constitution level. This means that your maximum health reduces the longer the fight goes on. Attacking the soul obelisk releases the energy allowing you to restore your Constitution level.
The Magister draws energy from the soul obelisk, restoring his lifepoints.
A corrupted obelisk appears that deals damage to the player. The obelisk can be attacked and destroyed to remove it.

extra.cheevo_details: Visit your house in Building Mode.

extra.tortle_combat_wolfgang_reaction: These are marvelous! Their smoothness and shine is perfect for me. Thank you kindly!
extra.tortle_combat_gustav_reaction: I am afraid that these might not be sufficiently structurally sound to withstand prolonged combat.
extra.tortle_combat_johann_reaction: I am sorry, friend. These knives and forks are not ideal as they will not allow me to fight enemies from a safe distance.
extra.tortle_combat_alfred_reaction: Alfred has been chewing on one slice of pizza ever since you arrived, which has since turned to mush. He really doesn't seem to need cutlery.

extra.tortle_combat_wolfgang_reaction: Please don't leave this thing around me for too long. Someone could get hurt.
extra.tortle_combat_gustav_reaction: If this were to break during fighting, my defensive capabilities would be compromised.
extra.tortle_combat_johann_reaction: The length of this instrument is excellent for engaging foes from far away. I shall take it!
extra.tortle_combat_alfred_reaction: After a painful minute of uncertainty, the rake handle falls to the ground. Alfred seems unimpressed.

extra.tortle_combat_wolfgang_reaction: This may be too rough of an implement for my fine sensibilities I am afraid.
extra.tortle_combat_gustav_reaction: Now this axe looks both durable and effective. I am sure that I will be able to depend on it. Great work!
extra.tortle_combat_johann_reaction: An axe such as this is more of a tool than a martial weapon, do you not think?
extra.tortle_combat_alfred_reaction: Alfred isn't paying attention. He drops the axe to the ground, where almost separates a rat from its tail.

extra.tortle_combat_wolfgang_reaction: How on earth would I fight with this? It is a creature with an independed mind. I surely could not force it to do my bidding.
extra.tortle_combat_gustav_reaction: If this is another animal you have brought to calibrate our teleportation device, I must say it looks even less appropriate than the rabbit.
extra.tortle_combat_johann_reaction: If I threw this at my enemies, perhaps it would be effective? No, that seems outlandish.
extra.tortle_combat_alfred_reaction: The chinchompa hops up to Alfred's shoulder. He seems content with this new friend.

extra.tortle_combat_wolfgang_reaction: Ever since gaining consciousness, I have been oddly obsessed with music. I would rather conduct others than play myself, though.
extra.tortle_combat_gustav_reaction: The planets would really need to align for this to win me any combat.
extra.tortle_combat_johann_reaction: Ah the lyre, instrument of choice of the modern bardic tortle. I myself favour the pipe organ. Neither are effective weapons.
extra.tortle_combat_alfred_reaction: Alfred accidentally snaps the last remaining string on the lyre as he steps on it.

extra.tortle_combat_wolfgang_reaction: This is very smooth. So smooth in fact that I conclude that no living creature could be hurt by it.
extra.tortle_combat_gustav_reaction: With this in my hands, I worry more for the safety of the creature than that of my enemies.
extra.tortle_combat_johann_reaction: Could I teach this animal to grab my foes and draw them in close with its appendages to get them over here? Perhaps, but ultimately unlikely.
extra.tortle_combat_alfred_reaction: Alfred doesn't even blink as the jellyfish rolls off his shell and leaves behind a thick layer of slime.

extra.tortle_combat_wolfgang_reaction: Now this is truly the least dangerous object you have brought to me. I do enjoy its touch though, somewhat.
extra.tortle_combat_gustav_reaction: This could indeed cause some damage, but how do I continue fighting once I have thrown it?
extra.tortle_combat_johann_reaction: A thrown weapon! I had not considered this. On second thought, it is rather uncomfortable to hold.
extra.tortle_combat_alfred_reaction: Alfred stares into the void as the snowball continues to melt.

extra.tortle_combat_wolfgang_reaction: You have thought of everything! We will not have to rely on ordering pizza going forward. Now where is that weapon you wanted to show me?
extra.tortle_combat_gustav_reaction: This could be used as a shield or a blunt weapon, depending on the situation. If only it had a cutting edge as well...
extra.tortle_combat_johann_reaction: Since starting a fire down here seems nigh impossible, this cooking implement seems to be but marginally useful.
extra.tortle_combat_alfred_reaction: You place the pan over Alfred's head to stop a leaky pipe from continuing to drop water on it. He stays as still as a rock.

extra.bslay_tactic_text: Fighting under the control of Jas, Kerapac is an extremely powerful dragonkin who wields multiple elder artefacts and will stop at nothing to achieve his goal.

When a player gets close to defeating Kerapac, he communes with the time altering elder artefact, the Needle. Using this power, Kerapac rewinds time and starts his onslaught again.

By doing so, he creates a new Time-thread. A version of Kerapac existing within the previous Time-thread will appear and attacks from the previous phases will play out at the same time during this new Time-thread.

Kerapac will smash his staff into the ground, causing a powerful attack to charge toward the player. The force of this hit can stun the player if they're struck by it.

Once the attack reaches the edges of the arena, Kerapac will draw it back toward him, causing any player caught in the crossfire to take a large amount of damage.

In Hard Mode, the force of Kerapac's attack will rip a hole in the current time thread which will seep damage to all players in the arena until closed.

Kerapac will jump up and hover in the air for a few seconds before slamming back toward the ground focused on where his target is currently.

If Kerapac lands on his target, he will pin them in place and apply continuous damage until they break free of his pin. Using the ability Freedom or Anticipation will stop Kerapac being able to pin you in place.

Kerapac will jump 3 times before resuming his attacks.
Kerapac will call upon the power of the Staff of Armadyl to cause a torrent of lightning waves to sweep across the arena.

In Hard Mode, Kerapac will push the needle one step too far, causing it to overcharge and cross over the Time-threads that Kerapac created previously.

An echo of Kerapac from each phase, along with an echo of the player will appear.

Kerapac, now tethering his life from the broken Time-threads, becomes immune to incoming attacks until the echos have been dealt with.

During this phase, Kerapac will be attacking all players with a barrage of powerful attacks.
In Hard Mode, all versions of Kerapac have a stacking buff called <col=E6DCB4>Fury</col>. For each stack, Kerapac gains a <col=FFFFFF>1%</col> damage increase for all attacks.

For each Time-thread, an echo of the player exists and is being targeted by an echo of Kerapac.

If Kerapac kills a player's echo, all versions of Kerapac gain 25 stacks of Fury. A player can jump into a Time-thread and then heal their echo up. Jumping into a Time-thread will cause the appropriate echo of Kerapac to start targeting the player.

Defeating an echo of Kerapac will lower the main Kerapac's shield but will also cause all versions of Kerapac to gain 50 stacks of Fury.

extra.bslay_tactic_text: A large, icy monster from the barren planet, Leng. Wen has summoned this titan terror to attack Senntisten from the south in hopes of reclaiming her kin, the elder eggs.

Shards of ice will slowly creep in from either side of the aqueduct, decreasing the size of the arena the further they creep. If they reach the players position, they will cause large amounts of damage and push the player in the direction they're creeping in.
A set of Glacyte will spawn on the aqueduct. Whilst unkilled, the Glacyte will shield the Arch-Glacor who will be immune to all damage.

The Arch-Glacor will send out a series of attacks that will strike the player with either <col=FFFFFF>melee, magic or ranged</col> damage. Each attack's damage will be reduced by the player using the correct protection prayer.

The player will be pushed to a small section of the arena by <col=FFFFFF>Creeping ice</col>. Once within this reduced area, an elemental beam will fire down from the sky and move constantly towards the players current location. After a period of time, the beam will split into two. Upon contact with the beam the player will take rapid damage.

The player will be pushed to a small section of the arena by <col=FFFFFF>Creeping ice</col>. The Arch-Glacor morphs into a giant frost cannon that targets the player and hit them for a massive amount of damage.

The player will be pushed to a small section of the arena by <col=FFFFFF>Creeping ice</col>. The Arch-Glacor will smash it's arms down either side of the players current position and unleash it's <col=FFFFFF>core</col>. This core will do rapid increasing damage to the player. Whilst the <col=FFFFFF>core</col> is active, the player must attack and break the arm in order to escape the damage from the <col=FFFFFF>core</col>.

extra.bslay_tactic_text: Fighting as Ful's champion, TzKal-Zuk awaits a challenger worthy to take him on.

TzKal-Zuk's connection to the earth around him causes a series of small-scale earthquakes. Remaining close to a quake's location will apply the <col=FFFFFF>Armour Break</col> debuff and cause a <col=FFFFFF>Geothermal Burn</col>.
TzKal-Zuk will thrust his sword into the player, causing a <col=FFFFFF>Geothermal Burn</col>.
TzKal-Zuk inflicts a searing pain that starts to reduce the target player's maximum life points.
TzKal-Zuk slams his target with an empowered hit for typeless damage.
TzKal-Zuk splits the room in two with a massive wall of flames.
TzKal-Zuk will cast a powerful magic attack and launch it toward his target for large damage upon impact. The target area will be engulfed in flames for a short period of time.

TzKal-Zuk draws forth a Conduit of Ful which begins to heat up the room. Using this heat source, TzKal-Zuk will cast Igneous Bomb at the target player. Severing TzKal-Zuk's connection with the Conduit will cause him to stagger and take 20,000 damage. In retaliation, TzKal-Zuk will send a massive attack back toward the target player.
Each time the target player severs the connection, TzKal-Zuk will become more enraged, casting Igneous Bomb at a faster rate.

TzKal-Zuk locks down sections of the arena and summons forth igneous creature as he channels.

Dealing with each igneous creature will charge the player, allowing them to stagger TzKal-Zuk as he charges his explosion.

The Ungael ritual site is a more economical, laid-back Necromancy training method.

However, Ungael experience rates are slightly lower than Um, and communion rituals cannot be performed here.

extra.slayer_description: Crawling hands are undead severed hands; fast and dexterous, they claw their victims. They can be found in the Slayer Tower, north-east of the entrance to Morytania.
Wolves are pack animals, so you'll always find them in groups. Watch out for their bite, it can be nasty. There are plenty to kill on White Wolf Mountain.
Cave bugs are like cave crawlers, except smaller and easier to squish; although, they still have a fondness for plants. They lurk in the dark beneath Lumbridge Swamp.
Cows are bigger than you, and they'll often hit hard but react fairly slowly. You can slaughter the ones in Lumbridge - I bet they are up to no good.
Birds aren't the most intelligent of creatures, but watch out for their sharp, stabbing beaks. Even the chickens in Lumbridge are after your blood, so get them before they get you.

These mindless creatures attack relentlessly once provoked. There is a core floating in their chest, and they can only be beaten by bursting this core wearing spiked gauntlets, once you have damaged them enough.

There are plenty of trolls not far from here. Head up to the cave between the Wall and Burthorpe castle if you want to find them. There are three sub-caves in there, one with shamans, another with warriors and another with rangers. Take your pick of how to take them down!
Goblins are mostly just annoying, but they can be vicious. Watch out for the weapons they sometimes carry. You can find them on the east side of the river here in Lumbridge.
Ghosts are undead, so not the easiest thing to find in populated areas. Try looking in the abandoned Draynor Manor.
Skeletons are undead, so Magic is your best bet against them. Skeletons can be found in the Lumbridge Catacombs.
Bats are rarely found on the ground, so you'll have to fight them while they're airborne. You can find some flying around in the Lumbridge Catacombs.
Zombies are undead, so be careful. You can find a variety of corpse fighters in the Lumbridge Catacombs or zombies in the sewers under Draynor village.
Spiders are often venomous and many varieties are camouflaged, too. I've seen plenty to the south-west of Lumbridge.
Birds aren't the most intelligent of creatures, but watch out for their sharp, stabbing beaks. Even the chickens in Lumbridge are after your blood, so get them before they get you.
Frogs will attack and move faster than the average human, but on the whole an experienced warrior can deal with a lot of them quite quickly. You can find them in the swamp to the south.
Cave slimes are the lesser cousins of jellies. Don't be fooled, though: they can still be dangerous, as they're often poisonous. Killing the ones beneath Lumbridge Swamp might be a good start.
Cave bugs are like cave crawlers, except smaller and easier to squish; although, they still have a fondness for plants. They lurk in the dark beneath Lumbridge Swamp.
Cows are bigger than you, and they'll often hit hard but react fairly slowly. You can slaughter the ones in Lumbridge - I bet they are up to no good.
Rats come in different sizes if you want a challenge or not. You can find the normal variety lurking around the castle grounds or head south into the swamp for giant rats.
Shadow warriors are dark and mysterious. They hide in the shadows, so be wary of ambushes. The basement of the Legends' Guild harbours these menaces.
Werewolves are feral creatures; strong and tough with sharp claws and teeth. The village of Canifis is home to many of them.

Bloodveld are strange, demonic creatures that use their long, rasping tongue to feed on just about anything they can find. If you wish to slay some, they live in the Slayer Tower to the north-west of Canifis.

Killerwatts store huge amounts of energy in their bodies, which is released if they are touched. You'll need to wear heavily insulated boots to counter this shocking effect, plus they can attack speedily with both magic and missiles. To access their cloudy plane, you'll need to explore Draynor Manor.
Crocodiles are large reptiles that live in the Kharidian Desert near water. River crocodiles are a bigger challenge than the ones found next to the ocean in the south east.
Ogres are brutal creatures, favouring large blunt maces and clubs. They often attack without warning. South of Yanille is an area ruled by these man-devourers.

Sea snakes are long and slithery, with a venomous bite. The larger ones are more dangerous, so keep an eye on your health. They live on isles far to the north-west, or, rather, in the sea caves of those isles.

Like other giants, moss giants often wield large weapons. Use fire spells to burn them to cinders before they can damage you. Strangely for giants, some have been seen at the end of the Varrock sewers.

Aberrant spectres are fetid, vile ghosts. The very smell of them will paralyse and harm you. A nosepeg will help you ignore their stink and make you fight at full capacity. Sniff them out in the Slayer Tower in Morytania.
Lesser demons are magic creatures, so they are weak to ranged attacks. Although they're relatively weak, they are still dangerous. Taverley Dungeon is home to these foul creatures.
Jungle horrors can be found all over Mos Le'Harmless. They are strong, aggressive and fight in packs, so watch out!
Turoths are large, vicious creatures with thick hides. You'll need a leaf-bladed weapon, broad arrows or a magic dart to harm them. You can find a nest of them in the Rellekka Slayer Caves.
Ankous are neither ghost nor skeleton, but a combination of both. Not much is known of these creatures. Perform some research in the depths of the Stronghold of Security.
Like other giants, ice giants often wield large weapons. Try using fire spells to melt them before they can hit you. Ice giants can be found underground to the south of Port Sarim.
Green dragons are the weakest dragons but they are still very powerful. Watch out for their fiery breath. These brutes live out in the Wilderness.

Jellies are nasty, cube-like gelatinous creatures that absorb everything they come across. Their acidic touch attacks in the same fashion as many magics, so prepare your armour beforehand. They keep parts of Rellekka Slayer Caves clean.
Infernal mages are dangerous spell users; beware of their Magic spells and go properly prepared. They have taken over an area upstairs in the Slayer Tower, plotting your doom.
Brine rats can be found in caves near to the sea. They are hairless, bad-tempered and generally unfriendly. If you have found Olaf's pirate treasure, you'll know where to find these targets.

Basilisks, like cockatrices, have a gaze which will paralyse and harm their prey. You'll need a mirror shield to protect you. Basilisks live in the Rellekka Slayer Caves, along with their cockatrice relatives.
Vampyres are extremely powerful beings. They feed on the blood of the living, so watch that you don't get bitten. Look in the woods of Morytania.

Molanisks are subterranean creatures. You can find them in caves deep below the ground. I heard that the goblins have recently had trouble with some, but they use a bell to lure them from the cave wall.
Pyrefiends are magical beings of fire and molten rock. They're quick and agile so try attacking them with a crossbow and bolts. You can find some fiends in the Rellekka Slayer Caves.

Shades are undead - The town of Mort'ton in Morytania is plagued by these creatures, so help if you can. There are some shades in the Stronghold of Security too, but you won't learn much from fighting those; stick to Mort'ton.
Earth warriors are an elemental warrior pieced together by rocks. Water washes them away easily so use spells of that type. They form from the rocks beneath Edgeville.
Cockatrices, like basilisks, have a gaze which will paralyse and harm their prey. You'll need a mirror shield to protect you. If you are brave enough, head to Slayer Caves east of Rellekka.
Otherworldly beings are ethereal creatures, making them weak to ranged attacks. They can be found haunting Zanaris.
Ice warriors are a kind of ice elemental. Thurgo the dwarf recently spotted some in the caves south of Port Sarim.

Ghouls aren't undead, but they are stronger and tougher than they look. They're also very cowardly and will run if they're losing a fight. They wait to ambush those entering the graveyard to the  North of Canifis.
Banshees use a piercing scream to shock their enemies; you'll need some earmuffs to protect yourself from them. Their cries echo throughout the Slayer Tower in Morytania.

Cyclopes are tricky giants, originally from the far-eastern lands. The brave warriors in the guild near Burthorpe have a collection of them; however, they are immune to anything other than melee attacks. Other specimens aren't so tough, and can be found in the God Wars Dungeon.
Grotworms have recently been spotted in a cave near Rimmington. The younger specimens haven't fully developed their mandibles yet, and will attack with some sort of acid spit.
Dogs are much like wolves; they are pack creatures that will hunt in groups. I've heard there are fearsome wild dogs beneath Karamja, or near Ardougne if you are less adventurous.
Cave crawlers are small and fast, often seen creeping around in the Rellekka Slayer Dungeon. Avoid their barbed tongue or you'll get poisoned.
Desert lizards are large reptiles with tough skin. They're cold-blooded, so dousing them with freezing water will finish them off after a tough battle. You can find them to the east of Sophanem.
Rock slugs are strange, stoney slugs, many of which have been seen in Rellekka Slayer Cave. You'll need to fight them until they are close to death, before finishing them off with salt.
Animated by Zemouregal, you can find bound skeletons swarming inside the crypts north of Fort Forinthry. You'll find earth magic effective at breaking down their ancient bones.

These pitiful creatures have no mind of their own and seek only the flesh of their enemies. You can find fetid zombies inside the crypts north of Fort Forinthry. You'll find using magic effective against them.

You can find armoured phantoms swarming inside the crypts north of Fort Forinthry. Their hateful spirits seek only violence. You'll find crush weapons effective at breaking down their ability to move.

These tortured spirits have been risen from the dead by Zemouregal and are bound to his will. You can find risen ghosts inhabiting the depths within the crypts north of Fort Forinthry, waiting for Zemouregal's command. You'll find bows effective against this target.
Undead raised by the necromancer Zemouregal. They lurk in the crypt north of Fort Forinthry.
You can find many types of undead around Gielinor, notably those festering inside the crypts north of Fort Forinthry.
You can find many types of demons around Gielinor, notably the abyssal demons infesting the Canifis Slayer Tower.
You can find many types of ghosts around Gielinor, notably those flooding the crypts north of Fort Forinthry.
You can find many types of zombies around Gielinor, notably those flooding the crypts north of Fort Forinthry.
You can find many types of skeletons around Gielinor, notably those flooding the crypts north of Fort Forinthry.
Abyssal demons are nasty creatures to deal with. They teleport around to confuse and trap their prey. They can be found within the Canifis Slayer Tower or inhabiting the Senntisten Asylum.
You can find dragons through Gielinor. Many types of them can be found within Brimhaven Dungeon.
Black dragons are the strongest of the chromatic dragons. They can be found resting within Taverley Dungeon. Using crossbows would be advantageous.
Green dragons are the weakest of the chromatic dragons and can be found west of the Dark Warriors Fortress. Using crossbows would be advantageous.

extra.slayer_description: Greater demons are relatively weak, however, you should still be careful as they can be dangerous. They can be found in Brimhaven Dungeon. Using crossbows would be advantageous.
Lesser demons are some of the weakest of all Avernic demons. They can be found inhabiting the Karamja Dungeon. Using crossbows would be advantageous.
Black demons are among the strongest of the Avernic demons. They can be found within the Brimhaven and Taverley dungeons. Using crossbows would be advantageous.

Like other giants, fire giants often wield large weapons. Learn to recognise what kind of weapon it is and act accordingly. They can be found in Brimhaven Dungeon. Using water spells would be advantageous.
Grotworms have been spotted in a cave near Rimmington. They will bite and attack with some sort of acid spit.
Dagannoth are large, sea-dwelling creatures that are very aggressive. You'll often find them in caves near seawater.
Aviansies can be found within the God Wars Dungeon north of Trollheim. As they fly, you'll find it difficult to reach them with melee weapons, so try using ranged or magic weapons instead.
Kalphites are large insectoids that live in hives under the Kharidian desert. You can find them southwest of Shantay Pass.
Hellhounds are Shakroth class Avernic demons, the lowest class of demons from Infernus. You can find them in Taverley Dungeon and will find slash weapons effective against them.

Aberrant spectres are fetid, vile ghosts. The very smell of them will paralyze and harm you. I would advise using a nose peg to avoid their stink. You would do well using a ranged weapon against them.

Ripper demons enjoy the bloodlust of battle, a sentiment I can agree with. They will expose your weaknesses, hitting you harder the worse your injuries are. They can be found in a fissure east of Al Kharid.
Camel Warriors use ancient magics to attack you. They can use cowardly disorientation magic to confuse you. You can find them in the deep desert, teach them a lesson in humility.

Acheron mammoths are honourable and proud beasts from the frozen north that know the true worth of battle. When they charge you, ensure you get out of the way. They can be found on an iceberg that is accessible from a dock east of Rellekka.

Living wyverns breathe a poison that will rapidly kill you unless you can freeze your blood using the glacial temperature of their home. But watch out; the colder you are, the harder their regular attacks will hit you. They can be found within the Asgarnia Ice Dungeon.
Dark beasts are large, dog-like predators with massively muscled bodies that protect them from crushing weapons. They can be found within the Mourner tunnels.

Ankou are undead beings that can be described as neither ghost nor skeleton, but a combination of both. Not much is known about these creatures, however, they make their home in the Stronghold of Security.
Skeletons are undead, so Magic is your best bet against them. Skeletons can be found in Edgeville Dungeon or Varrock sewers.
Wolves are pack animals, so you'll always find them in groups. Watch out for their bite, it can be nasty. There are plenty to kill on White Wolf Mountain.
Kalphite are large insects that live in hives under the desert sands. You can best enter their hive south-west of Shantay Pass, but try not to go too deep.

Mogres are a type of aquatic ogre that is often mistaken for a giant mudskipper. You have to force them out of the water with a fishing explosive. You can find them on the peninsula to the south of Port Sarim.
Ghosts play tricks and japes upon those entering Taverley Dungeon, so put them to rest. If you are after a bigger challenge you can find some stronger ghosts in the Stronghold of Security.

Bears are tough creatures and fierce fighters, so watch out for their powerful claws. Bears have been spotted west of Gunnarsgrunn near the mysterious ruins. I heard a rumour of a stronger type of bear down a rift to the east of Varrock.
Zombies are undead, so using magic against them is preferred. You should be able to find them roaming in the tunnels beneath Edgeville.
Hill giants use crude weapons or tools so prepare accordingly. There is a colony of them, deep inside the Edgeville tunnels; all good folk will approve if you clean it out.

Cave slimes are the lesser cousins of jellies. Don't be fooled, though: they can still be dangerous as they're often poisonous. You'll do Lumbridge a favour if you kill the slimes in Lumbridge Swamp caves.
Hobgoblins are larger and stronger then their brethren. There is a peninsula, south-west of Falador, where these creatures have a hideout.
Flesh crawlers are scavengers and will eat you and anyone else, given the chance. Save the weak by killing these creatures in the Stronghold of Security.
Catablepon are cow-like, magical creatures that mainly live in the Stronghold of Security. Beware their weakening glare; cutting off their head could help.

Wall beasts are really much larger creatures, but you'll only see their arms. You'll want something sharp on your head to stop them grabbing you. The geology of the caves beneath Lumbridge Swamp favours these creatures.
Ice warriors are a kind of ice elemental. Thurgo the dwarf recently spotted some in the caves south of Port Sarim.
Grotworms have recently been spotted in a cave near Rimmington. They will bite and attack with some sort of acid spit. Be careful - they are very aggressive.
Frogs will attack and move faster than the average human. You can find frogs in the Lumbridge swamp and if you venture into the swamp caves you can find giant frogs.
Minotaurs are large, man-like creatures, but you'll want to be careful of their horns. I hear they have set up camp under in the Stronghold of Security.

Spiders are often venomous and many varieties are camouflaged, too. I've seen plenty to the south-west of Lumbridge. If you are up for a challenge you can find stronger spiders down in the Stronghold of Security.
Scorpions are almost always venomous and usually found in groups. Last I heard you can find some scorpions in the Stronghold of Security.
Cockroaches are resilient creatures often found in dark and damp places. They have been spotted in the Stronghold of Player Safety to the south.
Bats are rarely found on the ground, so you'll have to fight them while they're airborne, which won't be easy with melee. They have been spotted in the Taverley dungeon.
Like other giants, ice giants often wield large weapons. Try using fire spells to melt them before they can hit you. Ice giants can be found underground to the south of Port Sarim.

Like other giants, moss giants often wield large weapons. Use fire spells to burn them to cinders before they can damage you. Strangely for giants, some have been seen at the end of the Varrock sewers.
Icefiends are beings of ice and freezing rock. They're quick and agile, so you'll want to be careful when getting close to them. Ice Mountain is infested with these pesky creatures.

Kurasks are large, brutal creatures with very thick hides. You'll need a leaf-bladed weapon, broad arrows or a magic dart to harm them. Kurask may be found in the caverns east of Rellekka. As they are so large, you may be able to kill them when they cannot reach you.

Like other giants, Fire giants often wield large weapons. Learn to recognise what kind of weapon it is and act accordingly. The smoke dungeon to the west of Pollnivneach has a population of these large and irritating creatures, so go smite them.

Gargoyles are winged creatures of stone. You'll need to fight them until they are close to death before breaking them apart with a rock hammer. There is a thriving population of Gargoyles in the Slayer Tower near Canifis.

Kalphites are large insects that live in hives under the desert sands. South-west of Shantay Pass they swarm and make themselves a nuisance. Enter deeper into the lair if you are looking for a suitable challenge.

Dagannoth are large, sea-dwelling creatures that are very aggressive. You'll often find them in caves near sea water. I can tell that you've seen the vile creatures, so you know where to go. Remember: they attack with missiles, so protect yourself accordingly.
Warped tortoises are creatures tainted by magical waste. They are vulnerable to an elven chime.
Trolls regenerate quickly but are still vulnerable to poisons. They usually use crushing weapons. Perhaps you should head to the snowy islands where these creatures are both fierce and aggressive.
Jungle horrors can be found all over Mos Le'Harmless. They are strong and aggressive, but you should be heroic enough to make short work of them.
Turoths are large, vicious creatures with thick hides. You'll need a leaf-bladed weapon, broad arrows, or a magic dart to harm them. Seek them out in the Rellekka Slayer Caves.

Cave horrors can be found in the caves under Mos Le'Harmless which favour the use of missiles or Magic. You will need a witchwood icon to fight them effectively. They drop the famous black Slayer mask, so the trip may be worth it.

Jellies are nasty, cube-like, gelatinous creatures which absorb everything they come across. Rellekka's caves are known to harbour these unnatural abominations. You can consider their attacks to be a form of Ranged and protect yourself with this in mind.
Lesser demons are weak to ranged attacks. Although they're relatively weak, they are still dangerous. Taverley's underworld is infested with these hellish pests.
Dust devils use clouds of dust, sand, ash and whatever else they can inhale to blind and disorientate their victims. They typically lurk in the smoky dungeon west of Pollnivneach.

Blue dragons aren't as strong as other dragons, but they're still very powerful. Watch out for their fiery breath. Taverley Dungeon has a clutch of these creatures, which it can be profitable to slay.

Elves are quick, agile, and vicious fighters who often favour bows and polearms. They also irritate me intensely, so slaughtering them is definitely a good thing. They live in the forests far, far to the west of human lands.

Aberrant spectres are fetid, vile ghosts. The very smell of them will paralyse and harm you. A nosepeg will help negate their stink and their attacks are most definitely magical in nature. You'll be able to make the world more fragrant if you kill the ones lurking in the Slayer Tower near Canifis.
Shadow warriors are dark and mysterious. They hide in the shadows, so be wary of ambushes. Apparently, a large number may be found lurking beneath the Legends' Guild.

Bloodveld are strange, demonic creatures. They use their long, rasping tongue to feed on just about anything they can find. Their tongue assaults physically, so using magic attacks might be the best choice. If you can stand being licked by a half-ton demon, you should take a trip to the Slayer Tower near Canifis.

Mutated zygomites are hard to destroy and attack with mainly magical damage. They regenerate quickly, so you will need to finish them off with fungicide. We have a bit of a problem with them here in Zanaris.
Infernal mages are dangerous spell users. Beware of their magic spells and go properly prepared to the Slayer Tower near Canifis.
Brine rats can be found in caves that are near the sea. They are hairless, bad-tempered and generally unfriendly. You may have spotted them while looking for pirate treasures.

Fever spiders are giant spiders that carry the deadly spider fever. If you don't want to catch it, I suggest you wear Slayer gloves to fight them. I've heard they cause problems in breweries, if you want to find some.

Basilisks, like cockatrices, have a gaze that will paralyse and harm their prey. You'll need a mirror shield to protect you. I am sure you know that there is a Basilisk colony in the Rellekka Slayer Caves.

Harpie bugs are pesky critters that are hard to hit. You need a lit bug lantern to distract them with its hypnotic light. They live on Karamja, near the coast, and just south-east of the narrow stretch of land which joins the two halves of the island.

Banshees use a piercing scream to shock their enemies. You'll need some earmuffs to protect yourself from them. Head to the Slayer Tower near Canifis to slay them, although I have heard rumours of tougher banshees in Pollnivneach.
Cave crawlers are small and fast, often hiding in ambush. Avoid their barbed tongue or you'll get poisoned. Squish them in droves at the Rellekka Slayer Dungeon near the golden tree.
Crawling hands are undead severed hands; fast and dexterous they claw their victims. Massacre these unnatural creations at the Slayer Tower near Canifis.

Bronze dragons are the weakest of the metallic dragons, but their bronze scales are far thicker than normal bronze armour. They lay in wait for you in Brimhaven Dungeon and the Chaos Tunnels. You'll be well served by taking a defence against their breath.

These tricky creatures burrow beneath the jungle north west of Oo'glog. Be careful, as these poisonous jungle wyrms like to use magical attacks from a distance, while they should be weak to stab attacks.

These foul creatures can be found throughout Meiyerditch and Darkmeyer in Morytania. They have a telepathic ability which enables them to dodge incoming attacks, so you'll need a weapon specially created to harm them.

Grifolapines live in a cave north-east of the Mage Training Arena. The creatures of that dungeon are coated in toxic fungus, so you should fight them from a distance, and dodge when they charge at you. The fungus helps them repair physical damage, so you might prefer using magical attacks.

Grifolaroos live in a cave north-east of the Mage Training Arena. The creatures of that dungeon are coated in toxic fungus, so you should fight them from a distance, although they'll try to hop over obstacles towards you. The fungus helps them repair physical damage, so you might prefer using magical attacks.

Fungal magi live in the upper levels of a cave north-east of the Mage Training Arena. The creatures of that dungeon are coated in toxic fungus, so you should fight them from a distance, and be prepared for their magical attacks. The fungus helps them repair physical damage, so you might prefer using magical attacks too.
Grotworms have recently been spotted in a cave near Rimmington. They will bite and attack with some sort of acid spit. Be careful - they are very aggressive.

Black demons are creatures that are weak to ranged attacks. They're the strongest type of demon and are therefore very dangerous. Prove yourself more dangerous by slaying these demons in their lairs beneath Taverley or Edgeville.

Spiritual warriors are fighters that have dedicated their souls to their deity; however, they still retain a fighter's weakness to Magic. They can be found fighting for the god whose cause they support. Kill them all and let their gods lament.

Scabarites are the followers of Scabaras and consist of anything from the lowliest dung beetle to the vilest scarab mage. They are most commonly found near and under Sophanem. They are traitorous creatures in the main, so commit genocide upon them.

Elves are quick, agile and vicious fighters that often favour bows, polearms and snide remarks. Their dedication to trees, bushes and music is an affront to me, so go and cause havoc in their vile villages. You'll need to travel far to the west.
Blue dragons aren't as strong as other dragons, but they're still very powerful. Watch out for their fiery breath! Taverley is home to these pests - I'm sure you'll enjoy murdering a few.

Kalphites are large insects that live in hives under the desert sands. Their Queen is rumoured to be quite powerful. Show people that you are a force to be feared by slaying her brood in the hive to the north-west.

Abyssal demons are nasty creatures to deal with. They aren't really part of this realm and are able to move very quickly to trap their prey. I'm sure you'd love a nice abyssal whip or two, so cull these demons in the Slayer Tower near Canifis.

Spiritual mages are the strongest of the spiritual guardians. They are devastating against warriors, but a smart ranger can often defeat them. They can be found in the icy God Wars Dungeon near Trollheim, supporting the cause of their chosen god. All these gods must be caused to lament; go slay their followers for me.

Nechryael are demons of decay that summon small-winged beings to help them fight their victims. I don't like them much, so kill a few as a personal favour. You can find them up to no good in the Slayer Tower near Canifis.

Aberrant spectres are fetid, vile ghosts. The very smell of them will paralyse and harm you, while a nosepeg will help ignore their stink. If you sniff carefully, you may be able to detect their aroma beneath the town's well. Kill a few of them, as they offend my nose.

Iron dragons are some of the weaker metallic dragons, but their iron scales are far thicker than normal iron armour. Brimhaven Dungeon has a few of these creatures in residence; I think they should be exterminated because they bore me.

Gargoyles are winged creatures of stone. You'll need to fight them until they are close to death, before breaking them apart with a rock hammer. They refuse to serve me, so smite them in my name. They are hiding out in the Slayer Tower near Canifis.

Bloodveld are strange, demonic creatures that use their long rasping tongue to feed on just about anything. They are rather robust but frankly feeble and have been seen in the Slayer Tower near Canifis, among other places. I never liked the look of them, so off you go and wipe them out.

Trolls regenerate quickly but are still vulnerable to poisons and usually use crushing weapons. I've nothing much against them but their ridiculous names. Unluckily for them, that's enough of a reason to put a few in their graves.

Greater demons are creatures that are weak to ranged attacks. Though not the strongest of demons, they are still dangerous. Prove yourself by doing away with them. If you don't know, a large number live in the Brimhaven Dungeon.

Like other giants, Fire giants often wield large weapons. Learn to recognise what kind of weapon it is and act accordingly. Prove that bigger isn't always better by defeating some. They lurk in the smoke dungeon, west of here, telling tales of your weakness.
Dagannoth are large, sea-dwelling creatures that are very aggressive. You'll often find them in caves near sea water. You'll cackle with glee if you set up a cannon and massacre them.

Hellhounds are a cross between dogs and demons, and are dangerous with a fierce bite. Although they are not cats, they deserve to die anyway. You'll be doing Gielinor a favour if you slay Hellhounds beneath Taverley.

Kurasks are large, brutal creatures with very thick hides. You'll need a leaf-bladed weapon, broad arrows, or a magic dart to harm them. Unluckily for kurasks, I am sending you to kill them. Luckily for you, kurasks thrive in the dungeons below Pollnivneach.

Dust devils use clouds of dust, sand, ash and whatever else they can inhale to blind and disorientate their victims. You'll be able to test your skills on them in the smoky dungeon to the west. Get going!

Turoths are large vicious creatures with thick hides. You'll need a leaf-bladed weapon, broad arrows, or a magic dart to harm them. I am sure you'll make yourself useful by killing the ones beneath our feet.
Cave horrors can be found under Mos Le'Harmless. You will need a witchwood icon to fight them effectively. If you want to make a nice Slayer helmet, you'll need the black mask they drop.

Basilisks, like Cockatrices, have a gaze which will paralyse and harm their prey. You'll need a mirror shield to protect you. Conveniently, you can have some combat fun with these brutes in the dungeon beneath the town well.
Warped tortoises are creatures tainted by magical waste. They are vulnerable to an elven chime. I know you have seen them in your adventures, so go crack some carapace.

Cave crawlers are small and fast, often hiding in ambush. Avoid their barbed tongue or you'll get poisoned. The ones in the caves below here have grown large and fat in blissful isolation - go and be a force of natural selection.

Banshees use a piercing scream to shock their enemies, so you'll need some earmuffs to protect yourself. I am sometimes disturbed in my sleep by their wails, so do me a favour and thin out those beneath us.

Red dragons are fearsome firebreathers, stronger than green or blue. I'm sure that you'll have fun pitting your skills against their claws in either Brimhaven's depths or the ravaged lands far to the north.

Terror dogs are, unsurprisingly, dogs that terrorise the weak. They are the servants of Tarn, who annoyed me when he was young. Be a force of vengeance for me by cleaning his lair of these pathetic servitors.

Aquanites are amphibious creatures that attract prey using the glowing lures on their heads. They attack stronger opponents from a distance with water magic, and dislike those who pray against it. You'll find these despicable, slimy creatures in the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon, in a chamber past the kurasks.

These tricky creatures burrow beneath the jungle north west of Oo'glog. Be careful, as these poisonous jungle wyrms like to use magical attacks from a distance, while they should be weak to stab attacks.
These things are the curse of the desert! Head north to find them on the hills above the Shantay Pass. Watch out for their vicious ranged attacks.

These warped jade vine creatures will not hesitate to use their environment to help them in combat if they cannot retaliate otherwise. The baby jadinkos are easiest to kill, but the males offer the greatest rewards. Ranged weapons made from vines are best against them.

These foul creatures can be found throughout Meiyerditch and Darkmeyer in Morytania. They have a telepathic ability which enables them to dodge incoming attacks, so you'll need a weapon specially created to harm them.

Grifolapines live in a cave north-east of the Mage Training Arena. The creatures of that dungeon are coated in toxic fungus, so you should fight them from a distance, and dodge when they charge at you. The fungus helps them repair physical damage, so you might prefer using magical attacks.

Grifolaroos live in a cave north-east of the Mage Training Arena. The creatures of that dungeon are coated in toxic fungus, so you should fight them from a distance, although they'll try to hop over obstacles towards you. The fungus helps them repair physical damage, so you might prefer using magical attacks.

Fungal magi live in the upper levels of a cave north-east of the Mage Training Arena. The creatures of that dungeon are coated in toxic fungus, so you should fight them from a distance, and be prepared for their magical attacks. The fungus helps them repair physical damage, so you might prefer using magical attacks too.
Grotworms have recently been spotted in a cave near Rimmington. They will bite and attack with some sort of acid spit. Be careful - they are very aggressive.

Without their master, Cres's automatons roam Guthix's chambers, attacking any who enter. They are programmed to use magic, melee or ranged and do a violent area-of-effect attack. Guthix's chambers may be reached via his shrine, or the excavation west of the Legends' Guild.
Aviansies can be found in the Godwars Dungeon north of Trollheim. As they are flying, you'll find melee attacks are not going to cut it.
Scorpions are almost always venomous and usually found in groups. Last I heard there was a large group near the mine north of Al Kharid.
Desert lizards are large reptiles with tough skin. They're cold-blooded, so dousing them with freezing water will finish them off after a tough battle.
Crocodiles are large reptiles that live near water. You'll want to have a stabbing weapon handy for puncturing their thick, scaly hides. These are desert beasts, so seek them there.
You can find corrupted creatures in the Sophanem Slayer Dungeon.
You can find soul devourers in the Sophanem Slayer Dungeon.
Profane scabarites are insect-like creatures that have abandoned their beliefs. They are causing issues for people of the desert. You will find them near the river Elid.
Scabarites are the followers of Scabaras and consist of anything from the lowliest dung beetle to the mightiest scarab mage. They are most commonly found near Sophanem, and under it.
Dark beasts are large, dog-like predators with massively muscled bodies that protect them from crushing weapons. You'll find them near the Temple of Light, attracted to the power of the Death Altar.
Abyssal demons are nasty creatures to deal with. They aren't really part of this realm and are able to move very quickly to trap their prey. The Slayer Tower is home to a number of these creatures.
Kalphites are large insects that live in hives under the desert sands. I am sure that, by now, you have seen them to the south-west of Shantay Pass.

Spiritual mages are the strongest of the spiritual guardians. They are devastating against warriors, but a smart ranger can sometimes defeat them. Of course, Prayer might serve you well, too. They can be found in the icy caverns near Trollheim, supporting the cause of their chosen god.
Nechryael are demons of decay that summon small winged beings to help them fight their victims. They can be found in the  Slayer Tower near Canifis.

Aberrant spectres are fetid, vile ghosts. The very smell of them will paralyse and harm you. A nosepeg will help ignore their stink and weak slayers might decide to pray when fighting them. They can be found in the Slayer Tower near Canifis and I have heard rumours that they also live beneath Pollnivneach in the desert.

Iron dragons are some of the weaker metallic dragons; their iron scales are far thicker than normal iron armour. Their fiery breath and sharp claws can be negated by a number of means. If you haven't visited Brimhaven Dungeon's depths then I advise you do - if only for the interesting creatures like these to kill there.
Gargoyles are winged creatures of stone. You'll need to fight them until they are close to death before breaking them apart with a rock hammer. Exterminate those in the Slayer Tower.
Black demons are weak to ranged attacks. They're still the strongest demon and very dangerous, however. Seek them out in the Edgeville or Brimhaven dungeons.
Steel dragons are dangerous and metallic, with steel scales that are far thicker than normal steel armour. As you are an accomplished slayer, I am sure you'll be able to deal with them easily.

Bloodveld are strange, demonic creatures. They use their long, rasping tongue to feed on just about anything they can find. Remember that their tongues are magical in nature but, moreso, they deserve to die.

Black dragons are among the strongest dragons and are very fierce. Watch out for their fiery breath. I am sure you will have seen them in your travels and have honed your techniques on lesser dragons.
Greater demons are weak to ranged attacks. Though not the strongest of the demons, they are still dangerous. Slaughter them easily in Brimhaven's depths, and revel in your power.
Suqahs can only be found on the mystical Lunar Isle. They use melee and magical attacks, and they often drop hide, teeth and herbs.
Like other giants, Fire giants often wield large weapons. Learn to recognise what kind of weapon it is and act accordingly. Remember the days when these were a challenge to you, and laugh.
Dagannoth are large, sea-dwelling creatures that are very aggressive. You'll often find them in caves near sea water. There is no joy so great as to cleanse these from the face of Gielinor.
Hellhounds are a cross between dogs and demons; they are also dangerous with a fierce bite. Make them know fear.
Dust devils use clouds of dust, sand, ash and whatever else they can inhale to blind and disorientate their victims. Good luck on obtaining a dragon chainmail from their dusty remains.

Warped terrorbirds are creatures tainted by magical waste and are vulnerable to an elven chime and may only be damaged when a chime has been used; look carefully to work out which. Their sonic attack is a Ranged attack but may be affected by ear defences.
Waterfiends are creatures of water that live under the Baxtorian Lake. Those followed by familiars are keen to slay these elemental forces.

Goraks are extremely aggressive creatures. They have been imprisoned on an alternate plane, which is only accessible by using the fairy rings. Be extremely careful: their touch drains life points as well as skills!

Skeletal wyverns are extremely dangerous and they are hard to hit with arrows, as they slip right through. To stand a good chance of surviving, you'll need some elemental shielding from their icy breath.
Mithril dragons are very dangerous opponents. They live beneath the Baxtorian Falls and devour most of those who seek to slay them. You are a battlemaster; test your skills.

The coldest of their kind, they are found on the Frozen Waste Plateau. As they are beings of ice, I've found that fire spells inflict far more damage against them.

Kal'gerion demons are powerful creatures that use both magic and melee. They reside near the Demonic Ruins. I would recommend you take cover when they smash the ground, or when they use magic to pull you towards them.

Lava strykewyrms are the most powerful of their kind. They attack with all combat styles and are weak to nothing. They can be found deep within the Wilderness to the south-west of the Lava Maze. I would watch your back while slaying them.
Dark beasts are large, dog-like predators with massively muscled bodies that protect them from crushing weapons. They can be found south of the Lava Maze.
You can find onyx dragons south east of Red Dragon Isle.
You can find hydrix dragons north west of the Lava Maze.
Revenant ghosts range from ghostly imps to dragons, they are all very powerful. They have the ability to heal themselves, so make sure you're prepared! These ghosts reside in the Forinthry Dungeon.
You can find soulgazers north east of the Graveyard of Shadows
You can find greater demon berserkers and ash lords west of the Lava Maze.
extra.slayer_name: greater demon berserkers and ash lords

extra.slayer_description: Abyssal savages can be found south of the Scorpion Pit
Abyssal beasts can be found east of the Lava Maze.
Abyssal lords can be found east of the Lava Maze.
Glacors were brought to this world by Lucien. They use magic, ranged and melee attacks. You can find in the snow west of here.

Living wyverns breathe a poison that will kill you rapidly unless you are freezing. But watch out; the colder you are the harder their regular attacks will hit you.  They can be found in the snow west of here.
Dark beasts are large, dog-like predators with massively muscled bodies that protect them from crushing weapons. We found some while mining the Mourner tunnels, in search of the Temple of Light.

Abyssal demons are nasty creatures to deal with. They aren't really part of this realm and are able to move very quickly to trap their prey. They can be found in Canifis Slayer Tower and in the Senntisten Asylum.
Gargoyles are winged creatures of stone. You'll need to fight them until they are close to death before breaking them apart with a rock hammer. They can be found in Canifis Slayer Tower.

Iron dragons are some of the weaker metallic dragons, with iron scales that are far thicker than normal iron armour. Their fiery breath and sharp claws can be negated by a number of means. Look for them in Brimhaven Dungeon.
Steel dragons are dangerous and metallic, with steel scales that are far thicker than normal steel armour. Look for them in Brimhaven Dungeon.

Black dragons are among the strongest dragons and are very fierce. Watch out for their fiery breath. I am sure you will have seen them in your travels and have honed your techniques on lesser dragons.
Greater demons are weak to ranged attacks. Though not the strongest of demons, they are still dangerous. There are some in Brimhaven Dungeon.
Black demons are weak to ranged attacks. They're still the strongest demon and very dangerous, however. Seek them out in the Edgeville or Brimhaven dungeons.
Mithril dragons are very dangerous opponents. There's some in the Ancient Cavern, north of where you'll find Kuradal. You are a battle master - test your skills.
Kalphites are large insects that live in hives under the desert sands. I am sure that, by now, you have seen them to the south-west of Shantay Pass.
Dagannoth are large, sea-dwelling creatures that are very aggressive. You'll often find them in caves near sea water. There is no joy so great as to cleanse these from the face of Gielinor.
The coldest of their kind, they are found beneath the Fremennik mountains. As they are beings of ice, I've found that fire spells inflict far more damage against them.

Aquanites are amphibious creatures that attract prey using the glowing lures on their heads. They attack stronger opponents from a distance with water magic, and dislike those who pray against it. They dwell in the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon, in a chamber past the kurasks.

These warped jade vine creatures will not hesitate to use their environment to help them in combat if they cannot retaliate otherwise. The baby jadinkos are easiest to kill, but the males offer the greatest rewards. Ranged weapons made from vines are best against them.

These foul creatures can be found throughout Meiyerditch and Darkmeyer in Morytania. They have a telepathic ability which enables them to dodge incoming attacks, so you'll need a weapon specially created to harm them.

Ganodermic beasts and runts live in the depths of a cave north-east of the Mage Training Arena. The creatures of that dungeon are coated in toxic fungus, so you should fight them from a distance. The fungus helps them repair physical damage, so you might prefer using magical attacks.

Without their master, Cres's automatons roam Guthix's chambers attacking any who enter. They are programmed to use magic, melee or ranged and can perform a violent area-of-effect attack. Guthix's chambers may be reached via his shrine, or the excavation west of the Legends' Guild.
Aviansie can be found in the God Wars Dungeon north of Trollheim. As they are flying, you'll find melee attacks are not going to cut it.
The Order of Ascension are magic users. It is strongly suggested you use ranged attacks. Their tactics can make them tough one-on-one, so bringing a friend along would be beneficial.
The airut are aggressive creatures from another world. They have powerful arms and attack with great vigour. Certain abilities can counter and stun them, however.
Elves are skilled fighters across all disciplines from whom you could learn a lot. I recommend challenging only one type of elf combatant at a time.

Muspah are creatures born of nightmares. Ancient magic is the most effective thing to use against them. You can find them by travelling to Freneskae. They'll be aggressive unless you wear your shard of Zaros.

The surviving subjects of Zaros's experiments. They have powerful charge attacks and fight in packs of four. You can find them by travelling to Freneskae. They'll be aggressive unless you wear your shard of Zaros.

Celestial dragons are one of the strangest dragons I assign. They use melee but also have a powerful dragonfire attack, as well as a fascinating ability to momentarily stop time. You can find them in the depths of Dragontooth Island.

Kal'gerion demons are powerful creatures that use both magic and melee. They reside in a resource dungeon near Daemonheim. I would recommend you take cover when they smash the ground, or when they use magic to pull you towards them.
Glacors were brought to this world by Lucien. They use magic, ranged and melee attacks. You can find them in an underground cavern on the Frozen Plateau.
Tormented demons are powerful creatures that use magic, ranged and melee attacks. They also have the ability to shield themselves. You can find them below the Tears of Guthix cave.

Edimmu are ghosts which failed to escape their body. They're ghosts and zombies, yet somehow different altogether. They use ranged attacks and are highly aggressive. You can find them in a resource dungeon, which the Meilyr clan in Prifddinas has access to.
Shadows are light creatures that have been corrupted by the Dark Lord. The Amlodd summon them to their section of the city in order to defeat them and then cleanse their cores.

Lava strykewyrms are the most powerful of their kind. They attack with all combat styles and are weak to nothing. They can be found deep within the Wilderness so I would watch your back while slaying them.
Adamant dragons are even more dangerous than mithril dragons. Look for them in Brimhaven dungeon, beneath a staircase north-west of the iron and steel dragons.

Rune dragons are even more dangerous than adamant dragons. I highly recommend you bring dragonbane ammunition to pierce their armour. To find them, you must travel to Kethsi via the World Gate in Arandar.
Crystal shapeshifters are deranged remnants of the elves on Tarddiad. They are quite mad and, according to Angof, beyond redemption. Show them mercy by ending their suffering.

Living wyverns breathe a poison that will kill you rapidly unless you are freezing. But watch out; the colder you are the harder their regular attacks will hit you.  They can be found in the Asgarnia Ice dungeon.

Ripper Demons are driven crazy by the scent of blood. They will hit you harder the worse your injuries are. And watch out; they can sometimes drop on you from above, which is lethal.  They can be found in a fissure near Al Kharid.
Camel warriors can use ancient magics to attack you. They also have the blessings of Akthanakos and can create powerful, disorientating mirages.  They can be found in the deep desert.
Acheron Mammoths are honourable yet powerful beasts from the frozen north. When they charge you, get out of the way! They can be found on an iceberg that is accessible from a dock near Rellekka.

You can find Chaos giants out in the Barendir tunnels, beyond Keldagrim. Be careful, as they can launch their Dragon throwing axe at range or take a swipe at you if you get close. Perhaps you could recover some.
You can find nightmare creatures on Freneskae, which can be accessed through the world gate.
You can find gemstone dragons beneath the gem mine in Shilo Village.
You can find corrupted creatures in the Sophanem Slayer Dungeon.
You can find soul devourers in the Sophanem Slayer Dungeon.
You can find the creatures of the lost grove within the lost grove, south of the poison waste.
You can find stalker creatures within Zamorak's hideout.
You can find a variety of dinosaurs on Anachronia.
You can find a variety of vile blooms on Anachronia.
You can find any type of Dragon around Gielinor.
You can find jungle strykewyrms in jungles, ice strykewyrms in icy environments and lava strykewyrms in hot environments.
You can find many types of demons around Gielinor.
You can find various creatures from the depths of Daemonheim lurking in sinkholes across Gielinor.
Nodon dragonkin are deeply intelligent creatures, armed with advanced siege weaponry. However, they are weak to dragonbane weapons. You can find them fighting for Jas in Senntisten.

You can find armoured phantoms swarming inside the crypts north of Fort Forinthry. Their hateful spirits seek only violence. You'll find crush weapons effective at breaking down their ability to move.

These tortured spirits have been risen from the dead by Zemouregal and are bound to his will. You can find risen ghosts inhabiting the depths within the crypts north of Fort Forinthry, waiting for Zemouregal's command. You'll find bows effective against this target.
You can find many types of undead around Gielinor, notably those festering inside the crypts north of Fort Forinthry.
Profane scabarites are insect-like creatures that have abandoned their beliefs. They are causing issues for people of the desert. You will find them near the river Elid.
